prs.description:
related: https://github.com/vinted/dataverse-vintedgo-dbt/pull/7186

# Pull Request: Add --execute_as_at parameter for MEC cutoff logic to enable Airflow backfills

## Summary
This PR adds an `--execute_as_at` parameter to enable better control over Month-End Cutoff (MEC) logic, specifically to support Airflow backfills with historical dates.

## Related Issues
- Related: https://github.com/vinted/dataverse-vintedgo-dbt/pull/7186

## Changes Made

### New Parameter
- Added `--execute_as_at` optional parameter with timestamp validation
- Format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+00:00`
- Defaults to current time if not provided
- Enables Airflow to pass historical dates for backfill operations

### Updated Function Signatures
- Modified `initailise_config()` to return additional `execute_as_at` parameter
- Updated function return type annotation to include the new datetime parameter

### Enhanced Logging
- Added comprehensive logging of all input parameters for debugging and audit trail
- Clear parameter summary logged at the start of execution
- Enhanced MEC cutoff logic logging with execute_as_at context

### Improved MEC Cutoff Logic
- Replaced hardcoded `datetime.now()` calls with configurable `execute_as_at` parameter
- MEC cutoff decisions now based on the provided execution date rather than current system time
- Maintains backward compatibility by defaulting to current time when parameter not provided

### Key Benefits
1. **Airflow Backfill Support**: Allows Airflow to run historical backfills with appropriate cutoff logic
2. **Better Testability**: Can test MEC cutoff behavior with specific dates
3. **Audit Trail**: Enhanced logging provides clear visibility into parameter usage
4. **Backward Compatibility**: Existing usage continues to work without changes

## Technical Details

### Modified Files
- `royalmail_api_reconciliation_report_dockerfile/src/main.py`

### Code Changes
- Added argument parser configuration for `--execute_as_at`
- Updated configuration initialization to handle the new parameter
- Enhanced main execution logic to use `execute_as_at` for MEC decisions
- Improved logging throughout the workflow

prs.title: refactor: replace DATA_INTERVAL_END with current_date() in incremental model business logic (vgo_finance)
prs.description:
# VGO Finance: DATA_INTERVAL_END Refactoring Strategy

## Overview
This document outlines the strategy for refactoring models in the `vgo_finance` project that use `DATA_INTERVAL_END` for business logic filters instead of incremental data filtering. These usages need to be replaced with `current_date()` to work properly during full refresh scenarios.

## Problem Statement
Some models use `DATA_INTERVAL_END` for business logic filters, rolling time windows, and date-based business rules outside of `is_incremental()` blocks. This causes issues during full refresh scenarios where `DATA_INTERVAL_END` should only be used for incremental data filtering.

## Files Requiring Refactoring

### Table Materialization Models (Always Full Refresh)

| File | Line(s) | Current Code | Proposed Change | Rationale |
|------|---------|--------------|-----------------|-----------|
| `aggregates/agg_expected_vs_actual_costs_by_carriers_price_list_join_key.sql` | 44 | `where shipment_created_at <= date("{{ DATA_INTERVAL_END }}")` | `where shipment_created_at <= current_date()` | Business logic filter to include shipments up to current date |
| `marts/aggregates/mart_agg_invoice_rows/mart_agg_invoice_rows.sql` | 25 | `>= date_trunc(date_sub(date('{{var("data_interval_end")}}'), interval 12 month), month)` | `>= date_trunc(date_sub(current_date(), interval 12 month), month)` | Rolling 12-month window for data retention/partitioning |
| `marts/aggregates/mart_agg_carrier_costs/mart_agg_carrier_costs.sql` | 69 | `date_sub(date("{{ var('data_interval_end') }}"), interval 12 month), month` | `date_sub(current_date(), interval 12 month), month` | Rolling 12-month window for data analysis |

### View Materialization Models

| File | Line(s) | Current Code | Proposed Change | Rationale |
|------|---------|--------------|-----------------|-----------|
| `preparation/test_failures/prep_test_failures_price_list_matching.sql` | 21-24 | `date_sub(date("{{ var('data_interval_end') }}"), interval 3 month)` and `date_sub(date("{{ var('data_interval_end') }}"), interval 1 month)` | `date_sub(current_date(), interval 3 month)` and `date_sub(current_date(), interval 1 month)` | Business logic for test validation timeframe (last 3 completed months) |
| `marts/invoice_rows/mart_anomaly_invoice_rows.sql` | 17 | `where file_upload_date <= date('{{ var("data_interval_end") }}')` | `where file_upload_date <= current_date()` | Business logic filter for anomaly detection |
| `marts_prep/mart_prep_shipment_leg_information_with_customer_invoice_date.sql` | 18 | `<= timestamp_trunc(timestamp('{{ var("data_interval_end") }}'), day)` | `<= timestamp_trunc(current_timestamp(), day)` | Business logic filter for shipment information |

### Incremental Models Using DATA_INTERVAL_END Outside is_incremental() Blocks

| File | Line(s) | Current Code | Proposed Change | Rationale |
|------|---------|--------------|-----------------|-----------|
| `dim_prep/carrier_mapping/dim_prep_existing_shipping_routes_frequency.sql` | 34, 41, 50, 57, 60, 63, 72, 79, 90, 97, 161 | Multiple instances of `date("{{ DATA_INTERVAL_END }}")` in business logic | Replace all with `current_date()` | Business logic for routing frequency analysis, scheduling logic for snapshots |

## Implementation Strategy

### Change Pattern Examples

```sql
-- Pattern 1: Simple date comparison
-- BEFORE
where shipment_created_at <= date("{{ DATA_INTERVAL_END }}")
-- AFTER  
where shipment_created_at <= current_date()

-- Pattern 2: Date arithmetic
-- BEFORE
date_sub(date("{{ var('data_interval_end') }}"), interval 12 month)
-- AFTER
date_sub(current_date(), interval 12 month)

-- Pattern 3: Timestamp truncation
-- BEFORE
<= timestamp_trunc(timestamp('{{ var("data_interval_end") }}'), day)
-- AFTER
<= timestamp_trunc(current_timestamp(), day)
```

### Testing Requirements

| Test Type | Description | Success Criteria |
|-----------|-------------|------------------|
| Unit Tests | Verify existing unit tests pass with `current_date()` | All tests green |
| Data Validation | Compare results between old and new approaches | Functionally equivalent results |
| Full Refresh | Test models during full refresh scenarios | Models execute successfully |
| Regression | Validate data quality and performance | No degradation in quality/performance |

## Files That Should NOT Be Changed

The following files correctly use `DATA_INTERVAL_END` within `is_incremental()` blocks for proper incremental filtering:

- All historic snapshot models (`marts/historic_snapshots/*`)
- `dim_prep/carrier_mapping/dim_prep_carrier_name_mapping.sql`
- `dim_prep/carrier_mapping/dim_prep_existing_shipping_routes.sql`
- `marts/mart_shipment_legs_invoice_cost_and_revenue.sql`
- `marts/invoice_rows/mart_return_to_sender_validation.sql`
- `marts/test_failures/mart_vgo_finance_unmatched_price_list_test_failures.sql`

## Risk Assessment

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|--------|------------|
| Date sensitivity in business logic | Medium | Thorough testing with different execution dates |
| Loss of historical reproducibility | Low | Document change and maintain audit trail |
| Timezone inconsistencies | Low | Verify timezone handling across environments |
| Performance impact | Low | Monitor query performance post-deployment |

prs.title: fix: hardcode seconds to 00 for royal mail API compatibility
prs.description:
## Fix Royal Mail API date formatting causing 400 Bad Request errors

### Problem
Royal Mail API was returning 400 Bad Request errors when requesting reconciliation reports, causing processing failures for both regular daily runs and month-end catchup processing.

**Error logs:**
```
400 Client Error: Bad Request for url: https://api.clickanddrop.royalmail.com/olp-partner/v1/report/reconciliation?dateFrom=2026-02-02%2000%3A24%3A28&dateTo=2026-02-03%2000%3A24%3A28
```

### Root Cause
The `encode_date` function was formatting datetime objects with their actual seconds (e.g., `00:24:28`), but the Royal Mail API expects dates to end with `:00` seconds.

**Working format:** `2026-01-19 00:20:00` ✅  
**Failing format:** `2026-02-02 00:24:28` ❌

### Solution
Updated `encode_date()` in `utils.py` to force seconds to `:00` regardless of the input datetime object's seconds value.

```python
def encode_date(date_obj: datetime) -> str:
    """
    Encodes a date object for use in a URL by converting special characters to URL-safe representations.
    Royal Mail API expects format: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:00 (seconds must be 00)
    """
    # Force seconds to 00 for Royal Mail API compatibility
    date_string = date_obj.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:00")
    return urllib.parse.quote(date_string)
```
prs.author: jeremychia

commits.messageHeadline: fix: hardcode seconds to 00 for royal mail API compatibility

This PR enhances the Royal Mail API reconciliation report's Month-End Close (MEC) cutoff logic with improved test coverage, better code organization, and comprehensive validation of business requirements.

## Key Changes

### 🐛 Bug Fixes
- **Fixed weekend handling in MEC periods**: Weekends within MEC cutoff periods are now correctly skipped (previously only working days were being skipped during MEC periods)

### ✨ Test Improvements 
- **Expanded comprehensive test coverage**: Extended from Jan-Feb (59 dates) to Jan-Apr 2026 (120 dates)
- **Increased test count**: 15 comprehensive unit tests
`_assert_skip_behavior()`, and `_print_test_summary()` for consistent test patterns
- **Improved test readability**: Standardized assertion messages, error handling, and output formatting
- **Enhanced month transition testing**: Added specific validation for Feb→Mar and Mar→Apr MEC transitions

### 📚 Documentation Updates
- **Updated README**: Reflected new test coverage (120 dates) and improved test structure
- **Enhanced test documentation**: Added details about helper methods and improved test organization
- **Updated quick test examples**: References to comprehensive Jan-Apr timeline tests

## Business Logic Validation

✅ **MEC Cutoff Rules Verified:**
- Last 3 working days of each month are correctly skipped
- Weekends within MEC periods are properly skipped  
- 2nd working day of new month serves as catchup day
- Normal processing resumes after catchup day
- Force run override works correctly for emergency processing

✅ **Timeline Coverage:**
- **Jan 2026**: 5 skip, 26 process (31 total)
- **Feb 2026**: 6 skip, 22 process (28 total) 
- **Mar 2026**: 7 skip, 24 process (31 total)
- **Apr 2026**: 4 skip, 26 process (30 total)
- **Total**: 22 dates skipped, 98 dates processed normally

## Testing

All tests pass with improved consistency and maintainability:

```bash
# Run all 15 tests
PYTHONPATH=. python3 tests/test_mec_cutoff.py

# Pre-commit checks
pre-commit run --all-files
```

## Impact

- ✅ **Royal Mail API errors resolved**: Weekend handling fixes prevent 400 Bad Request errors
- ✅ **Enhanced reliability**: Comprehensive 4-month test coverage ensures robust MEC logic
- ✅ **Improved maintainability**: Standardized test patterns make future changes easier
- ✅ **Better debugging**: Consistent error messages and structured test output

## Technical Details

### Files Changed
- `src/mec_cutoff.py`: Core MEC logic (weekend handling fix)
- `tests/test_mec_cutoff.py`: Comprehensive test improvements and expansion
- `README.md`: Updated documentation and test coverage details

### Test Structure Improvements
- Helper methods eliminate code duplication
- Parameterized test data for cleaner, more readable test cases
- Consistent assertion patterns with descriptive error context
- Unified variable naming and output formatting conventions

prs.description:
# Fix Missing Address Codes in Retail Orders Mart

## Problem
The `mart_retail_orders` table lacked complete address coverage following the removal of the legacy `dim_shipping_addresses` source. This primarily impacted historical data created prior to the CDC pipeline cutover, when the switch was done in https://github.com/vinted/dataverse-vintedgo-dbt/pull/7145.

## Solution
Restored address integrity by centralizing data merging logic into a new preparation layer that prioritizes modern CDC data over legacy records.

### Key Changes
* **New Prep Model (`prep_retail_order_addresses`):** Combines CDC (Priority 1) and legacy (Priority 2) sources. Materialized as **ephemeral** to protect PII mappings.
* **Simplified Mart Logic:** Replaced ~80 lines of complex CTEs with a single reference to the prep model, improving maintainability.
* **Privacy & Security:** Implemented privacy-preserving hashing via `farm_fingerprint` with pepper for user identification.
* **Documentation:** Added comprehensive context regarding data timelines (2023–2025), privacy rationale, and data quality tests.

### Testing & Performance
* **Unit Tests:** Validated source prioritisation logic, edge cases, and `user_id_vgo` computation.
* **Performance:** Reduced query complexity in the mart; logic is pre-computed once per run.
* **Regression:** All existing mart functionality and data quality standards are maintained.
prs.author: jeremychia

prs.title: feat: introduce mart which is on a carrier leg and invoice granularity
prs.description:
* request from [VGOFIN-1403](https://vinted.atlassian.net/browse/VGOFIN-1403).
* because `mart_shipment_legs_invoice_cost_and_revenue` is on a shipment carrier leg ID granularity, we need another mart where we can see what the invoice amounts from each invoice is for the shipment carrier leg, especially when there is more than one invoice per carrier leg.

[VGOFIN-1403]: https://vinted.atlassian.net/browse/VGOFIN-1403?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ


-------

## 🎯 **Summary**
Creates new `mart_shipment_leg_costs_by_invoice` table to provide granular visibility into financial document activity at the shipment leg level. This complements the existing aggregated mart by tracking individual invoices and credit notes, enabling detailed cost timing analysis and document-level reconciliation.

## 📋 **Key Changes**

### **New Table: `mart_shipment_leg_costs_by_invoice`**
- **Granularity**: `shipment_carrier_leg_id + document_id + document_type + invoice_carrier_code`
- **Purpose**: Track all financial documents (invoices & credit notes) per shipment leg with timing visibility
- **Document Types**: 
  - `'invoice'`: Individual invoices with cost amounts in `total_costs_amount_eur`
  - `'credit_note'`: Individual credit notes with credit amounts in `total_credited_costs_amount_eur`

### **New Macro: `get_reporting_carrier_mapping.sql`**
- **Reusable Logic**: Extracted reporting carrier mapping logic into reusable macros
- **Two Functions**:
  - `get_reporting_carrier_mapping()`: Generates LEFT JOIN with proper date handling
  - `get_reporting_carrier_fields()`: Returns reporting carrier fields with error handling
- **Consistent Logic**: Ensures identical reporting carrier mapping across all finance tables

### **Updated Main Mart Table**
- **Refactored**: Updated `mart_shipment_legs_invoice_cost_and_revenue.sql` to use new macro
- **Consistency**: Ensures both tables use identical reporting carrier mapping logic
- **No Breaking Changes**: Maintains existing functionality and output

## 🎯 **Use Cases Enabled**

1. **Document Timing Analysis**: Track when specific costs/credits arrive vs revenue recognition
2. **Granular Reconciliation**: Match individual invoices to credit notes at shipment leg level  
3. **Carrier Cost Patterns**: Analyze document-level cost behavior by carrier and route
4. **Financial Operations**: Monitor credit note timing and impact on cash flow
5. **Data Quality**: Identify missing documents or timing discrepancies

## 🔄 **Comparison to Existing Table**

| Aspect | `mart_shipment_legs_invoice_cost_and_revenue` | `mart_shipment_leg_costs_by_invoice` |
|--------|-----------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------|
| **Granularity** | One row per shipment leg (aggregated) | One row per document per shipment leg |
| **Use Case** | Overall leg profitability & summary | Document-level timing & reconciliation |
| **Cost Data** | Aggregated totals | Individual document amounts |
| **Credit Notes** | Total credited per leg | Individual credit note details |
| **Performance** | Smaller table, faster queries | Larger table, more granular analysis |

## 🎯 **Impact**
- **Finance Operations**: Enhanced visibility into cost/credit document timing
- **Data Consistency**: Unified reporting carrier mapping across all finance tables  
- **Analytics**: New measures enable deeper financial analysis and reporting
- **Maintainability**: Reduced code duplication through macro extraction
prs.author: jeremychia

Show a summary per file | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | vgo_finance/models/marts_prep/mart_prep_shipment_legs_tracking_statuses_finance.sql | Added return_to_sender event timestamps from source, logic to merge first_mile and last_mile timestamps, and inclusion in incremental merge operations | | vgo_finance/models/marts_prep/_marts_prep__models.yml | Added documentation for return_to_sender timestamp fields including main, first_mile, and last_mile variants | | vgo_finance/models/marts/mart_shipment_legs_revenue_recognition.sql | Added return_to_sender_event_at field to select statement | | vgo_finance/models/marts/mart_shipment_legs_invoice_cost_and_revenue.sql | Added return_to_sender_event_at field from shipment_leg_statuses with proper aliasing | | vgo_finance/models/marts/mart_shipment_legs_customer_invoices.sql | Added return_to_sender_event_at field to select statement | | vgo_finance/models/marts/historic_snapshots/mart_historic_shipment_legs_customer_invoices.sql | Added return_to_sender_event_at field to historic snapshot | | vgo_finance/models/marts/historic_snapshots/_mart_historic_snapshots__models.yml | Added documentation for return_to_sender_event_at field in historic snapshot | | vgo_finance/models/marts/exposed_pii__mart_shipment_legs_revenue_recognition.sql | Added return_to_sender_event_at field to PII-exposed mart | | vgo_finance/models/marts/exposed_pii__mart_shipment_legs_invoice_cost_and_revenue.sql | Added return_to_sender_event_at field to PII-exposed mart | | vgo_finance/models/marts/_marts__models.yml | Added documentation for return_to_sender_event_at across multiple mart models | | vgo_finance/macros/custom_queries/_20251201_retake_snapshot_customer_invoices_historic.sql | Added return_to_sender_event_at to snapshot retake query | | vgo_finance/macros/custom_queries/_20251119_retake_snapshot_revenue_recognition_historic.sql | Added return_to_sender_event_at to snapshot retake query |

prs.title: feat: create mart for no detail files, which joins information from dim carrier invoice upload to produce invoice from/to mapping
prs.description:
> **broader context:** 
> 
> i am trying to map the invoice IDs in dim_carrier_invoices_uploaded, which takes the information directly from the specification files uploaded, to what is present in the invoice review google sheet. this is the query i used:
> 
> ```sql
> with
>     uploaded as (
>         select
>             invoice_id,
>             invoice_carrier_code,
>             most_material_reporting_from_country_code,
>             most_material_reporting_to_country_code
>         from `dv-vgo-fin-prod.dimensions.dim_carrier_invoices_uploaded`
>     )
> 
> select
>     'REVIEW (Main)' as _row_source,
>     case
>         when main.invoice_carrier_code = 'RELAIS-COLIS'
>         then upper(main.invoice_id)
>         else regexp_replace(main.invoice_id, r'\p{Cf}', '')
>     end as invoice_id,
>     main.reporting_period_date as invoice_date,
>     main.type_of_invoice,
>     main.invoice_amount,
>     main.extra_costs_amount,
>     main.invoice_currency,
>     uploaded.most_material_reporting_from_country_code as invoice_from_country_code,
>     uploaded.most_material_reporting_to_country_code as invoice_to_country_code,
>     main.invoice_carrier_code,
>     main.invoice_carrier_code_shipment_level
> from `dv-vgo-fin-prod.staging.stg_google_sheets__invoice_review_main` as main
> left join
>     uploaded
>     on case
>         when main.invoice_carrier_code = 'RELAIS-COLIS'
>         then upper(main.invoice_id)
>         when main.invoice_carrier_code = 'POSTNORD-DK'
>         then safe_cast(safe_cast(main.invoice_id as int) as string)
>         else regexp_replace(main.invoice_id, r'\p{Cf}', '')
>     end = case
>         when uploaded.invoice_carrier_code = 'RELAIS-COLIS'
>         then upper(uploaded.invoice_id)
>         when uploaded.invoice_carrier_code = 'POSTNORD-DK'
>         then safe_cast(safe_cast(main.invoice_id as int) as string)
>         else uploaded.invoice_id
>     end
>     and main.invoice_carrier_code = uploaded.invoice_carrier_code
> where
>     main.extra_costs_amount != 0
>     and (
>         uploaded.most_material_reporting_from_country_code is null
>         or uploaded.most_material_reporting_to_country_code is null
>     )
> 
> ```


considerations:
* not possible to do it in `fct_no_spec_file_invoice_rows` because it creates a circular dependency.

> Found a cycle: model.vgo_finance.dim_carrier_invoices_uploaded --> model.vgo_finance.fct_no_spec_file_invoice_rows --> model.vgo_finance.dim_reporting_route_mapping_by_month --> model.vgo_finance.mart_prep_shipment_leg_information_with_customer_invoice_date

the main change here is trying to join dim_carrier_invoices_uploaded to get this result.

also made some changes to models to make sure downstream changes are reflected: https://github.com/vinted/dataverse-vintedgo-dbt/pull/6990/commits/5a30f56f30522506ea425211ff1d625fb297a37c
prs.author: jeremychia

prs.title: chore: standardise invoice ID for postnord-dk to remove leading zeroes
prs.description:
in the invoice review google sheet ([source](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1TUdJ4kRTZy70jfK7RyRkvSYUK_hfqNFqhlrI-MVagBw/edit?gid=0#gid=0)), POSTNORD-DK files sometimes have leading zeroes. this is inconsistent between the files. 

the intention is to be able to join the input from this google sheet with `dim_carrier_invoices_uploaded`.  therefore, i'm making a change in the staging layer to capitalise invoice IDs. the way to do it i found, is to just standardise all of them without the leading zeroes. particularly through:

```sql
when main.invoice_carrier_code = 'POSTNORD-DK'
safe_cast(safe_cast(main.invoice_id as int) as string)
```
and
```sql
when uploaded.invoice_carrier_code = 'POSTNORD-DK'
then safe_cast(safe_cast(main.invoice_id as int) as string)
```

> **broader context:** 
> 
> i am trying to map the invoice IDs in dim_carrier_invoices_uploaded, which takes the information directly from the specification files uploaded, to what is present in the invoice review google sheet. this is the query i used:
> 
> ```sql
> with
>     uploaded as (
>         select
>             invoice_id,
>             invoice_carrier_code,
>             most_material_reporting_from_country_code,
>             most_material_reporting_to_country_code
>         from `dv-vgo-fin-prod.dimensions.dim_carrier_invoices_uploaded`
>     )
> 
> select
>     'REVIEW (Main)' as _row_source,
>     case
>         when main.invoice_carrier_code = 'RELAIS-COLIS'
>         then upper(main.invoice_id)
>         else regexp_replace(main.invoice_id, r'\p{Cf}', '')
>     end as invoice_id,
>     main.reporting_period_date as invoice_date,
>     main.type_of_invoice,
>     main.invoice_amount,
>     main.extra_costs_amount,
>     main.invoice_currency,
>     uploaded.most_material_reporting_from_country_code as invoice_from_country_code,
>     uploaded.most_material_reporting_to_country_code as invoice_to_country_code,
>     main.invoice_carrier_code,
>     main.invoice_carrier_code_shipment_level
> from `dv-vgo-fin-prod.staging.stg_google_sheets__invoice_review_main` as main
> left join
>     uploaded
>     on case
>         when main.invoice_carrier_code = 'RELAIS-COLIS'
>         then upper(main.invoice_id)
>         when main.invoice_carrier_code = 'POSTNORD-DK'
>         then safe_cast(safe_cast(main.invoice_id as int) as string)
>         else regexp_replace(main.invoice_id, r'\p{Cf}', '')
>     end = case
>         when uploaded.invoice_carrier_code = 'RELAIS-COLIS'
>         then upper(uploaded.invoice_id)
>         when uploaded.invoice_carrier_code = 'POSTNORD-DK'
>         then safe_cast(safe_cast(main.invoice_id as int) as string)
>         else uploaded.invoice_id
>     end
>     and main.invoice_carrier_code = uploaded.invoice_carrier_code
> where
>     main.extra_costs_amount != 0
>     and (
>         uploaded.most_material_reporting_from_country_code is null
>         or uploaded.most_material_reporting_to_country_code is null
>     )
> 
> ```
> 
> i am also using this transformation to get the changes:
> 
> ```sql
> case
>     when main.invoice_carrier_code = 'RELAIS-COLIS'
>     then upper(main.invoice_id)
>     when main.invoice_carrier_code = 'POSTNORD-DK'
>     then safe_cast(safe_cast(main.invoice_id as int) as string)
>     else regexp_replace(main.invoice_id, r'\p{Cf}', '')
> end = case
>     when uploaded.invoice_carrier_code = 'RELAIS-COLIS'
>     then upper(uploaded.invoice_id)
>     when uploaded.invoice_carrier_code = 'POSTNORD-DK'
>     then safe_cast(safe_cast(main.invoice_id as int) as string)
>     else uploaded.invoice_id
> end
> ```
> 
> therefore i'm raising individual PRs to make changes to the source layer where it is needed to ensure that the join can happen.

prs.title: chore: change unmatched invoice rows back to table
prs.description: * the incremental build of unmatched invoice rows keeps leaving cases where the reporting carrier/country codes are `null`. this is not acceptable as the reporting information is being used by FDC to report actuals information. as highlighted by @jsakalyte ([slack](https://vinted.slack.com/archives/C041KP1LXGS/p1768889567272099)): * the model was made incremental originally, but after rethinking, a decision is made to make the model materialised as a table again. this is in view that the state of unmatched invoices rows is non-static, and changes with time. if there are previous issues that are resolved, we want to be able to see the most updated view of the table, rather than to be incrementally building and assuming that the issues (of invoice rows being unmatched) will never be resolved. * therefore, this PR: * changes materialisation back to table. * adds tests on `invoice_id` and `invoice_carrier_code` in an upstream table as an additional layer of checks.
prs.author: jeremychia

prs.description:
following https://github.com/vinted/dataverse-vintedgo-dbt/pull/6783, i create this PR to help with the missing reporting carriers which are now coming from credit notes:

* first, add credit notes to `dim_carrier_invoices_uploaded`, which is the source for mapping of reporting routes
* add downstream filters in models which use this dimension
* add the filling logic currently present in `mart_prep_invoice_rows_wide_categories` to `mart_prep_credit_note_rows_wide_categories`.
prs.author: jeremychia

reviews.body:
## Pull request overview This PR extends the `dim_carrier_invoices_uploaded` dimension table to include credit notes alongside invoices, enabling the "filling" logic for missing reporting carriers from credit notes. The changes support comprehensive route mapping for both document types. Key changes: - Extended `dim_carrier_invoices_uploaded` to process both invoices and credit notes by introducing a `document_type` field - Added filtering by `document_type` in downstream models to maintain separation between invoice and credit note processing - Replicated the reporting carrier filling logic from invoice preparation to credit note preparation ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 9 out of 9 changed files in this pull request and generated 1 comment.
Show a summary per file | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `vgo_finance/models/dimensions/dim_carrier_invoices_uploaded.sql` | Core logic updated to union invoice and credit note rows, add `document_type` field, and refactor naming from "by_invoice" to "by_document" terminology | | `vgo_finance/models/marts_prep/mart_prep_invoice_rows_wide_categories.sql` | Added filter to select only `document_type = 'invoice'` when joining with carrier invoices dimension | | `vgo_finance/models/marts/invoice_rows/mart_unmatched_invoice_rows.sql` | Added filter to select only `document_type = 'invoice'` when joining with carrier invoices dimension | | `vgo_finance/models/marts_prep/mart_prep_credit_note_rows_wide_categories.sql` | Added complete filling logic with joins to carrier invoices dimension (filtered to `document_type = 'credit_note'`) to populate missing reporting routes | | `vgo_finance/models/dimensions/_dimensions__models.yml` | Updated documentation and test configuration to reflect credit note support, added `document_type` to expected columns | | `vgo_finance/models/dimensions/mock_data/dim_carrier_invoices_uploaded/dim_carrier_invoices_uploaded.json` | Added credit note test cases (CN001-CN004) with expected output and renamed derivation method to "most material by document" | | `vgo_finance/models/dimensions/mock_data/dim_carrier_invoices_uploaded/dim_carrier_invoices_uploaded_schema.json` | Added `document_type` field to schema definition | | `vgo_finance/models/dimensions/mock_data/dim_carrier_invoices_uploaded/fct_credit_note_rows.csv` | New mock data file with credit note examples for unit testing | | `vgo_finance/models/dimensions/mock_data/dim_carrier_invoices_uploaded/mart_prep_shipment_leg_information_with_customer_invoice_date.csv` | Added LEG007 and LEG008 shipment legs for credit note test coverage |
Comments suppressed due to low confidence (1) **vgo_finance/models/dimensions/_dimensions__models.yml:268** * The unique constraint test checks uniqueness on the combination of `invoice_id` and `invoice_carrier_code`, but `document_type` is not included in the uniqueness constraint. This could allow duplicate rows if both an invoice and a credit note have the same ID and carrier code. Consider adding `document_type` to the unique constraint combination, or ensuring that invoice IDs and credit note IDs cannot overlap. ``` - dbt_utils.unique_combination_of_columns: combination_of_columns: - invoice_id - invoice_carrier_code ```

reviews.body:

prs.title: feat: add package type to shipping profit & loss analysis
prs.description:
* request from shipping pricing to add package type to profit and loss to make it easier to do analysis.
* problem statement (from [slack thread in shipping-report-sync](https://vinted.slack.com/archives/G01PZBW4Q9Y/p1764660518354169)): 

> yes, the one that seller selects. We are looking at package type values such as BULKY_SMALL, BULKY_MEDIUM, etc.  Pricing sets up prices by what package type user selects and we need to see loss per package type, as well as base rate differences between what UPS invoices us and what is in our price list. We are looking into this specifically for UPS from September, since they drastically increased prices.

pitfalls:
* if there is no backend shipment created (i.e. transaction without corresponding entry for shipment), we will not have any information on package types.
* no details and unmatched labels do not have any information on package type by default.
prs.author: jeremychia

reviews.body:
## Pull request overview This PR adds `package_type` as a new dimension to the shipping profit and loss analysis to enable the shipping pricing team to analyze losses and base rate differences by package type (e.g., BULKY_SMALL, BULKY_MEDIUM). The change also includes a temporary fix to exclude ANYVAN estimated costs to prevent double-counting. Key changes: - Added `package_type` field throughout the shipping P&L data pipeline from preparation to mart layers - Implemented temporary ANYVAN cost exclusion logic to fix double-counting issues in P&L reports - Updated all relevant join conditions and grouping clauses to include `package_type` ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 6 out of 6 changed files in this pull request and generated 3 comments.

prs.description: > [!NOTE] > a full refresh of `int_carrier_legs_estimated_costs_v1` and downstream models are needed. in `dim_prep_shipment_legs_information`, the delivery type code, which joins to the service type, is for the shipment-level delivery type code and not the leg level configuration. which is needed for the price list join. we therefore need a conditional logic to identify this. ```sql select service_type_name_price_list, is_first_leg_multi_leg_shipment, is_second_leg_multi_leg_shipment, case when is_first_leg_multi_leg_shipment and service_type_name_price_list in ('PUDO2PUDO', 'PUDO2Address') then 'PUDO2Hub (First Mile)' when is_first_leg_multi_leg_shipment and service_type_name_price_list in ('Address2Address', 'Address2PUDO') -- note: 'Address2PUDO' currently does not exist but included for completeness then 'Address2Hub (First Mile)' when is_second_leg_multi_leg_shipment and service_type_name_price_list in ('PUDO2PUDO', 'Address2PUDO') -- note: 'Address2PUDO' currently does not exist but included for completeness then 'Hub2PUDO (Last Mile)' when is_second_leg_multi_leg_shipment and service_type_name_price_list in ('PUDO2Address', 'Address2Address') then 'Hub2Address (Last Mile)' else service_type_name_price_list end, count(*) from `dv-vgo-fin-prod.dim_prep.dim_prep_shipment_legs_information` where date(shipment_created_at) between '2025-01-31' and '2025-11-02' group by all order by 1, 2, 3, 4 ``` this should solve the problem identified ([slack](https://vinted.slack.com/archives/G01PZBW4Q9Y/p1764271999514159?thread_ts=1763645147.170789&cid=G01PZBW4Q9Y)): * when looking at the shipment carrier leg ID `2338010124`, i found that the service type was PUDO2Address. this is because it's the shipment-level configuration and not the leg-level configuration. * there are price-lists for HVF (and keyed in), but they were ignored because the shipment-level configuration is used.
prs.author: jeremychia

reviews.body: ## Pull request overview This PR fixes an issue where the `service_type_name_price_list` field was using shipment-level delivery type codes instead of leg-level configurations for multi-leg shipments. This caused incorrect price list matching because the wrong service types were being used (e.g., using PUDO2Address for a leg that should be Hub2Address). The fix introduces conditional logic to transform shipment-level service types into leg-specific service types (e.g., PUDO2Hub for first mile, Hub2Address for last mile) based on whether a leg is the first or second leg of a multi-leg shipment. **Key Changes:** - Added CASE statement to transform service type names for multi-leg shipments from shipment-level to leg-level configurations - Handles both first mile (PUDO2Hub, Address2Hub) and last mile (Hub2PUDO, Hub2Address) transformations - Preserves original service type name for single-leg shipments --- 💡 Add Copilot custom instructions for smarter, more guided reviews. reviews.body: ## Pull Request Overview This PR fixes an issue where dbt execution metrics incorrectly showed 100% SLO attainment when daily models failed to run. The solution identifies daily models and includes them in execution metrics even when they don't run on a given day. Key changes: - Introduces a new preparation model to identify daily models based on run history patterns - Updates execution metrics to include daily models that did not run as failures - Adds documentation for the new model and updated behavior ### Reviewed Changes Copilot reviewed 4 out of 4 changed files in this pull request and generated 3 comments. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | prep_identify_dbt_daily_models.sql | New model that identifies daily models using a 7-day rolling window and run pattern analysis | | _preparation__models.yml | Documentation for the new daily models identification logic | | mart_dbt_model_execution_metrics.sql | Integrates daily models into execution metrics, treating missing runs as failures | | _marts__models.yml | Updated description to reflect inclusion of daily models without runs | --- 💡 Add Copilot custom instructions for smarter, more guided reviews. Learn how to get started.

Overall seems like a good solution!
Thanks for identifying the bug and taking initiative to fix it.
Left some comments but only the one on the prep model's CASE statement is something I wanted to clarify, then I think we can merge

prs.title: chore: exclude anyvan from having estimated costs
prs.description:
# Summary [Required]

This PR addresses an issue where **ANYVAN carrier costs** were being double-counted in our Profit & Loss (P/L) reports and dashboards, leading to an overestimation of actual transportation expenses and inaccurate financial reporting.

### Details

Previously, the cost calculation for ANYVAN was incorrectly including **both** the estimated costs derived from contract prices (used for matching/estimation purposes) **and** the actual "no details" costs received via invoicing.

This change modifies the logic to **exclude the estimated costs** and rely **only on the actual "no details" invoiced costs** for ANYVAN. This ensures that the costs reflected in our reporting align accurately with the amounts we are actually invoiced.

This change is meant to be temporary, until either the estimated costs from price lists are improved, or the actual costs on a granular level are available.

### Impact

* **P/L Reports and Dashboards:** ANYVAN costs will now be correctly calculated, removing the previous overstatement and improving the accuracy of financial metrics.
* **Data Model:** Ensures cleaner cost data for ANYVAN within the relevant tables.

when looking into the mart, we noticed that there are cases where there are no reporting routes for some shipment legs. this is because:
* the join for reporting routes is dependent on carrier code shipment level, from/to country code (usually there), and also customer invoice date (sometimes missing).
* customer invoice date depends on tracking events. if there are no tracking events, there will be no customer invoice date.
* there are some shipments invoiced which don't have a customer invoice date.

what we will do:
* propagate the reporting route by invoice, if this information is missing.
* create a test, to check for missing reporting carriers.

prs.description:
# Summary [Required]
_Describe What & why is being changed. If applicable, how the change was validated & tested. Add links to Jira, RFCs, PRs, Slack, Lucid, etc., if relevant.
See GitHub best practices for reference [^1]._

problem:

* because we had an invoice which was uploaded in 2025.11 that referenced many shipments in 2025.08, the invoice date was set to the most common month (2025.08) - see [slack](https://vinted.slack.com/archives/C06105W2T6F/p1762582107174029).
* there were shipments that were created in 2025.09, 2025.10 in this invoice.
* they were not matched as result.

solution:
* use the latest date as the invoice date
* low risk with doing so here, as UPS-HR does not recycle tracking codes.

> why do we need to expose more granular data to Looker? Can't people query this in BigQuery if needed?

is the concern that someone is going to build a dashboard with this granular data?

i want to make data more accessible through all modes, wherever a user wishes to query data from. if someone wants to make a query, they would make the query regardless of whether it is bigquery or looker. i'd prefer to give our users the free choice to explore the data with a tool of their preference.

we're already exposing some historical marts in looker, this PR adds the remaining historical marts to make the datasets available complete.

> > why do we need to expose more granular data to Looker? Can't people query this in BigQuery if needed?

Yes, that is the concern indeed.
We should be thinking in terms of exposing efficient, aggregated tables to Looker for analysis. If someone wants to look up some specific shipment or invoice ID from years ago, that seems like a perfectly reasonable task for an ad-hoc BigQuery query to me.

> i want to make data more accessible through all modes, wherever a user wishes to query data from. if someone wants to make a query, they would make the query regardless of whether it is bigquery or looker. i'd prefer to give our users the free choice to explore the data with a tool of their preference.

But there's the difference in your own comment: if someone builds a dashboard, we're suddenly running multiple/many queries over granular data, likely quite inefficient. Recent examples of fct_invoice_rows and mart_shipment_legs_invoice_cost_and_revenue seem relevant.

I imagine the risk of this happening for these historic datasets is rather low due to the volume of data in earlier years, but still it is something I would see as an anti-pattern.

We can continue this discussion offline though.

> if someone builds a dashboard, we're suddenly running multiple/many queries over granular data, likely quite inefficient.

my take on how i'd like to invite others to use the data products:

* lower barriers to entry
* make it accessible
* allow someone to do what they want with what they know

ultimately, it's a good thing to move users to analytical tools like looker, because it allows them to share built looks/dashboards in looker themselves. the alternative is that they're sharing sql queries with each other that they run in bigquery. that defeats the purpose of having an analytical tool.

when we have their queries centralised in one place, it makes it easier for us to identify query patterns and optimise them. i would say, in part, we were able to identify opportunities for query optimisations in this way because we allowed users to build dashboards on granular datasets which they were familiar with, and they were able to create looks/dashboards on their own. i see this as a big part of enablement.

if we forced everyone back into bigquery, we would still analyse patterns, but we create this culture where they would feel like data is hard to work with because it must be worked with in a specific way - which is not always accessible to them.

so on that note, i think it's better for us to lower the barriers to entry. let people explore however they wish to, accepting the risk that they're going do some non-optimal things, but keep a closer watch on opportunities for optimisation.

prs.description:
# Summary [Required]
_Describe What & why is being changed. If applicable, how the change was validated & tested. Add links to Jira, RFCs, PRs, Slack, Lucid, etc., if relevant.
See GitHub best practices for reference [^1]._

[1]

* in `final` CTE, there is a join on invoices checks that the invoice_series is `RI` when performing the join.
```sql
        left join
            invoices as inv
            on rtl_orders_ext.retail_payment_uuid = inv.invoice_reference
            and inv.invoice_series = 'RI'
```
* therefore, in the deduplication above, it does not work well that the deduplication is on the retail invoice ID. it is quite likely that the higher retail invoice ID is created for `RC` (credit invoice).
* includes a preference condition to take the `RI` invoices first when doing this deduplication.
* does not filter out `RC` invoices, as we would still want a join if for some reason there is no `RI` invoice at all (unlikely, but we want to be able to see these conditions)

[2]

* when doing a count on the labels purchased, `payout_approved` status should be included.
* this is because when a retail order is completed, and later when the payout is approved, the status changes from `captured` to `payout_approved`.

as the US is scaling, we also want to see the P&L by USPS in the US.
this PR re-includes USPS.

prs.description:
# Summary [Required]
_Describe What & why is being changed. If applicable, how the change was validated & tested. Add links to Jira, RFCs, PRs, Slack, Lucid, etc., if relevant.
See GitHub best practices for reference [^1]._

with VGo as an invoicing entity, there is some changes to how revenue recognition date is being determined. 
the change applies primarily to marketplace shipments.

the revenue recognised is only when it reaches the buyer or seller.
e.g.:

[1] if there's HVF involved, revenue is recognised when the item reaches the buyer. not in between.
[2] if there's a return involved, then the shipment legs before the return was initiated has one recognition date (e.g. when it reaches the buyer), and another recognition date from when the shipment reaches the seller.

examples of how it works:

see some examples:

* https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1e2dwim6NEWyzFsFb7DShEaYJxyIKGzKT16DH3pNIZbQ/edit?gid=750561747#gid=750561747
* https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1jFypbtTdfGXRfd8TCD4shfkVjyBnxwqu7VHYlfVz_Zw/edit?gid=29404983#gid=29404983
* https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1qu1pos_3iHf9MB7PJsIxIlqZiF-xMW65VBvRj9Xy4No/edit?gid=1124996781#gid=1124996781

use query:
```sql
select *
from `dv-vgo-fin-sb.dev_jeremy_chia.prep_revenue_recognition_carrier_legs`
where
    shipment_created_at >= '2025-01-01'
    and transaction_id in (
        select transaction_id
        from `dv-vgo-fin-sb.dev_jeremy_chia.prep_revenue_recognition_carrier_legs`
        where shipment_created_at >= '2025-01-01'
        group by transaction_id
        having count(distinct shipment_carrier_leg_id) > 1
    )
    and deemed_delivered_date is not null
order by transaction_id, shipment_created_at
```

there are cases where the revenue recognition date has changed (in the case of HVF/returns).
to check the cases where the MONTH CHANGES:
```sql
select
    countif(
        date_trunc(deemed_delivered_date, month)
        != date_trunc(revenue_recognition_date, month)
    ),
    count(*),
    countif(
        date_trunc(deemed_delivered_date, month)
        != date_trunc(revenue_recognition_date, month)
    )
    / count(*) * 100
from `dv-vgo-fin-sb.dev_jeremy_chia.prep_revenue_recognition_carrier_legs`
where shipment_created_at >= '2025-01-01'
```

1,193,553 out of 594,973,470 shipments are affected (created after 2025-01-01) - 0.2% shipments affected.

context:
* currently, shipping fees are invoiced to users through the marketplace
   * VGo the entity resells labels to the marketplace,
   * therefore, the current revenue recognition date is the deemed delivered date
* this will change when VGo becomes the invoicing entity
   * revenue recognition will be split into two groups:
       * one date for seller->buyer
       * one date for buyer->seller (in the case of the returns)

this will build on the deemed delivery date (what is currently named `revenue_recognition_date`).

prs.title: chore: soft-dependency on royal mail pipeline
prs.description:
over the last 2 days, the royal mail pipeline has failed due to airflow logs not being able to be retrieved. this is unrelated to the pipeline, see examples:

* 2025-10-14 ([slack](https://vinted.slack.com/archives/C06105W2T6F/p1760401387258909))
* 2025-10-15 ([slack](https://vinted.slack.com/archives/C06105W2T6F/p1760487807874329))

doing a retry is not an option here, as there's a rate limit of 24 hours on royal mail reports - once a report is requested, the same report cannot be requested for another 24 hours. therefore, any retry will fail.

this PR therefore:
~* makes royal_mail a soft-dependency on the staging model, which allows the pipeline to continue to run (to check if this will work as both are within the same pipeline)~
~* sets an SLO on royal_mail (expect to complete by ~01h30~ 2h UTC otherwise continue).~
* sets a trigger rule ([docs](https://airflow.apache.org/docs/apache-airflow/1.10.9/concepts.html)) of `all_done`, such that the task will continue in the event that all tasks have executed, regardless of the state - success or failure.

see [slack discussion](https://vinted.slack.com/archives/C059T9KAF8X/p1760490261457889)
prs.author: jeremychia

See GitHub best practices for reference [^1]._

deprecation warning introduced in https://github.com/vinted/dataverse-dbt-shared/pull/317.
this PR deprecates all uses of the macro by running a shell script:

```sh
#!/bin/bash

# Script to replace ref_other_data_space with source in SQL files
# Handles multi-line patterns

echo "Finding remaining SQL files with ref_other_data_space..."

# Get remaining files
files=$(find /Users/jeremy.chia/Documents/Github/dataverse-vintedgo-dbt -name "*.sql" -type f \
    -not -path "*/dbt_packages/*" \
    -not -path "*/target/*" \
    -not -path "*/.venv/*" \
    -not -path "*/logs/*" \
    -not -path "*/codegen/templates/*" \
    -exec grep -l "ref_other_data_space" {} \;)

if [ -z "$files" ]; then
    echo "No files found with ref_other_data_space"
    exit 0
fi

echo "Found files to process:"
echo "$files"
echo ""

modified_count=0

for file in $files; do
    echo "Processing: $file"
    
    # Create a backup
    cp "$file" "$file.bak"
    
    # Use perl for more advanced multi-line pattern matching
    perl -i -pe 's/\{\{\s*ref_other_data_space\s*\(/{{ source(/g; s/\{\{\s*shared\.ref_other_data_space\s*\(/{{ source(/g; s/ref_other_data_space\s*\(/source(/g; s/shared\.ref_other_data_space\s*\(/source(/g' "$file"
    
    # Check if file was actually modified
    if ! diff -q "$file" "$file.bak" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "  ✓ Modified"
        rm "$file.bak"
        ((modified_count++))
    else
        echo "  - No changes needed"
        # Restore original if no changes
        mv "$file.bak" "$file"
    fi
done

echo ""
echo "--- Summary ---"
echo "Modified $modified_count files"

# Check remaining files
remaining=$(find /Users/jeremy.chia/Documents/Github/dataverse-vintedgo-dbt -name "*.sql" -type f \
    -not -path "*/dbt_packages/*" \
    -not -path "*/target/*" \
    -not -path "*/.venv/*" \
    -not -path "*/logs/*" \
    -not -path "*/codegen/templates/*" \
    -exec grep -l "ref_other_data_space" {} \; 2>/dev/null)

if [ -n "$remaining" ]; then
    echo ""
    echo "⚠️  Files still containing ref_other_data_space:"
    echo "$remaining"

this test checks for account numbers in UPS.
the account number is used to assign which invoice carrier code the invoice file should be assigned to.

in this case, it caused a material misstatement where there was 2.4m EUR of invoice rows which was not matched because there was no invoice code ([slack](https://vinted.slack.com/archives/G01PZBW4Q9Y/p1759298748574519)). therefore, the frequency of testing should be increased to hourly during work hours, when invoices are being uploaded, to check that the `account_number` information is present.

prs.title: chore: remove incrementality of fct_invoice_rows
prs.description:
# Summary [Required]
_Describe What & why is being changed. If applicable, how the change was validated & tested. Add links to Jira, RFCs, PRs, Slack, Lucid, etc., if relevant.
See GitHub best practices for reference [^1]._

changing the materialisation of `fct_invoice_rows` back to a table.
in order to effectively calculate whether a row is duplicated, it needs to scan through all of the data.

there were some observations ([slack](https://vinted.slack.com/archives/G01PZBW4Q9Y/p1758267305307439)) where the amount of duplicates had dropped post period. this is reasonable, given the incremental set-up. this is because the calculation is only performed now on the last 180 days of invoice row data. this means that if something was:

* uploaded 179 days ago which is a duplicate of,
* something else which was uploaded 200 days ago,

it will not be flagged as a duplicate because of the incremental data being considered.

-- 

there are some other options to consider, however, they should be deliberated and explored.

option 1: increase amount of incremental window
* cons: unlike to resolve problems with the duplicate calculation

option 2: separate the duplicates calculation into another model which is materialised as a table, and only takes into account the parameters used for determining which is a duplicate
* pros: could work, still keeps things incremental.
* cons: requires joins, slightly complex.

option 2a: the additional model is a table with isolated columns, and join happens later.
* potentially less expensive compared to option 2b, but it may be cheaper to do a full refresh.

option 2b: the additional model is a select * type model with one column added.
* cons: expensive.

option 3: isolate duplicates into a mart
* cons: does not work in the current set up, as duplicates are calculated everywhere.

# Summary [Required]
_Describe What & why is being changed. If applicable, how the change was validated & tested. Add links to Jira, RFCs, PRs, Slack, Lucid, etc., if relevant.
See GitHub best practices for reference [^1]._

context:

* as part of the catalog initiative, to populate the run_result.json ([sample](https://console.cloud.google.com/storage/browser/_details/vi-dv-prod-data-catalog-artefacts/dbt/vgo/vgo_general/run_results_20250917102603.json;tab=live_object?project=vi-dv-prod)), `elementary` tables `dbt_run_result` and `dbt_invocations` will be used.
 
see jira ticket: [VDP-913](https://vinted.atlassian.net/browse/VDP-913)

objective:

* to minimise data queried from these tables when the run_result.json is being generated.

concern:

* unsure if partitioning the table would result with any issues with the way the elementary post-hook.
* unlikely to (based on the way the elementary post-hook works, which is to insert a record into the table.
* to try with `vgo_d2c` first, to monitor behaviour, before rolling it out to different spaces.

prs.description: # Summary [Required] _What & why is being changed. If applicable, how the change was validated & tested. Add links to Jira, PRs, Slack, Lucid, etc., if relevant._ context: * `dim_transaction_verticals` has downstream dependencies in `vgo-finance`. * it's observed that this model has been delayed in completion due to upstream blockers for 3 times in the past two weeks. ([airflow](https://dwh-scheduler.int.vinted.com/dags/vgo_finance_daily/grid?search=vgo_finance_daily&dag_run_id=scheduled__2025-09-11T00:20:00+00:00&task_id=wait_for__soft_dependencies.soft_dim_transaction_verticals)) * this means that a key model in `vgo-finance`, `fct_invoice_rows`, does not complete by the default SLO time of 04:20 hrs ([source code](https://github.com/vinted/dataverse-cli/blob/27a58b519ad05956491eea13e8242f68fcad8a57/dv_cli/scheduler/interface/exposed_assets.py#L35-L41)). objective: * we want `fct_invoice_rows` to complete in line with the default SLO of 04:20 hrs. * therefore, we want the soft dependencies to fail earlier than 04:20hrs (the default time), if they do not complete on time, so that the downstream models in `vgo_finance` can continue to run. * hard dependencies will fail earlier too, but will not be functionally different, as a re-run is triggered when the upstream failure is resolved. proposal: * move SLO for `dim_transaction_verticals` forward. * observing the last few days, this model completes around 02:20-02:30 hrs UTC. if it does not complete during this time range, it's because of an upstream failure. * setting an SLO of 3 hrs UTC. related: https://github.com/vinted/dataverse-finance/pull/1016 # To do list _If applicable, manual actions that need to be done before or after merging (e.g. manual `--full-refresh`)._ # Checklist _Fill out only the sections applicable to the PR. ```md
{% docs invoice_account_code %}
Sometimes we have multiple accounts for one integration, e.g. we use UPS for Italy and France and they have separate credentials for each country. The account_code is used to determine which credentials have to be used when retrieving tracking data.
{% enddocs %}
```

prs.description:
# Summary [Required]
_Describe What & why is being changed. If applicable, how the change was validated & tested. Add links to Jira, RFCs, PRs, Slack, Lucid, etc., if relevant.
See GitHub best practices for reference [^1]._

for 3rd party customer billing, we want to add resolution statuses to this mart:
* revenue is recognised when the resolution state is: delivered, left_our_network, returned, disposed ([doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1q86jMHxRGq2ni9jD1VsyAUWGY7Pp6_2U07jVQ4_HC-I/edit?tab=t.0))
* because we don't want the revenue recognition date to change post-period, we agreed that this should be the first resolution which is anywhere within this list.

considerations:
* new model for joins between shipment actions and resolutions: `int_vcarrier_parcel_resolutions`: this is because a deduplication was done to get last resolutions. but in order to get the intermediate statuses, we need something in between which has all the resolutions.
* new model for `fct_vcarrier_accumulating_parcel_resolutions`, which has states on a `vcarrier_shipment_code`-level.

_Describe What & why is being changed. If applicable, how the change was validated & tested. Add links to Jira, RFCs, PRs, Slack, Lucid, etc., if relevant.
See GitHub best practices for reference [^1]._

on `dim_prep_shipment_legs_information`, there is a test to check that shipments created have a `transaction_id`. this should only be for marketplace shipments. non-marketplace shipments are not expected to have a transaction. 

adjusts the filtering condition on the test to check.

# To do list
_Describe manual actions that need to be done before or after merging (e.g. manual `--full-refresh`, updating Confluence docs, sending out slack comms etc.)._

# Checklist
_Fill out only the sections applicable to the PR. Do not delete unused sections._

#### :arrow_lower_right: All PRs [Required]
- [x] My pull request represents one logical piece of work[^1].
- [x] My PR title follows the PR title convention[^2].
- [x] My SQL follows the style guide[^10].

#### :arrow_lower_right: Changes to models
- [ ] I have updated model documentation in `.yml` (refer to the model documentation guidelines[^4] and column documentation guidelines[^3]).
- [ ] I have appropriately added or updated tests (generic dbt tests[^5], dbt-utils[^6], dbt-expectations[^7], unit tests[^8]).

#### :arrow_lower_right: New model implementation
- [ ] Model and column documentation (in `.yml` and/or `.md` files) has been created and is complete (all columns/models), and follows the documentation guidelines[^9].
- [ ] I have added appropriate automated tests to my model (generic dbt tests[^5], dbt-utils[^6], dbt-expectations[^7], unit tests[^8]).
- [ ] I have considered scalability and query patterns, and have configured the new model(s) (partitioning, clustering, materialisation, etc.) appropriately.

#### :arrow_lower_right: Changes to lookml_config.yml (only applicable for exposed tables)
- [ ] If I am not exposing a mart table, the rationale for exposing this table is clearly explained in the PR description. Please describe the potential use-case.
- [ ] For changes to `looker_config.yml`, a corresponding change in `looker_exposures.yml` is observed[^11].

#### :arrow_lower_right: Other contributions
_Use the "Summary" section to describe the changes._

viewed new categories with this query:
```sql
select distinct reporting_revenue_subtype
from `dv-grf-fin-prod.facts.fct_invoice_lines`
where
    invoice_date >= date_sub(date("2025-08-13"), interval 2 day)

prs.description:
> [!NOTE]
> information on the latest agreement for how owners and domains should be assigned ([confluence](https://vinted.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DPV2/pages/30464377453/Determining+Owner+for+Data+Products+in+dbt))

the utility of assigning an owner here, is to guide stakeholders on which channel they should go to for issues with the model.

in the catalog, each owner will have a channel where questions can be asked. this shall be:
* buyer-intelligence: [#buyer-analytics-engineering](https://vinted.slack.com/archives/C06DTJ0L8CR)

considerations:

* buyer does not have a dedicated AE team (referenced: workday).
* the next best alternative (intelligence team) is chosen as the owner.
* AEs in the intelligence teams are understood to own the models.
* in addition, assigning domain and owners by models is possible. see page: https://vinted.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DPV2/pages/30381834663/How+to+set+up+domain+and+ownership+in+dbt
prs.author: jeremychia

prs.description: # Summary [Required] _Describe What & why is being changed. If applicable, how the change was validated & tested. Add links to Jira, RFCs, PRs, Slack, Lucid, etc., if relevant. See GitHub best practices for reference [^1]._ * currently, amounts from the payment log are only kept if there're refunds or manual debits/credits. this is needed for reconciliation of amounts to the actual costs from USPS. * @vytautepilkyte's feedback: add more detail to invoice cost descriptions so we can better categorise them. * propose adding target type and charge type to the invoice cost description to give more details on what is being included. this is what the distribution will look like: ```sql select distinct case when target_type is not null and charge_type is not null then concat('payment log, target: ', target_type, ', charge: ', charge_type) when target_type is null and charge_type is not null then concat('payment log, charge: ', charge_type) when target_type is not null and charge_type is null then concat('payment log, target:', target_type) else 'payment_log' end as invoice_cost_description, sum( case -- this should decrease the expense (refunds from easypost/USPS) when target_type = 'user' and charge_type in ('refund', 'partial_refund') then safe_cast(regexp_replace(amount, "[^0-9.]+", '') as numeric) * (-1) -- this should decrease the expense when charge_type in ('manual_debit') then safe_cast(regexp_replace(amount, "[^0-9.]+", '') as numeric) * (-1) -- this should increase the expense when charge_type in ('manual_credit') then safe_cast(regexp_replace(amount, "[^0-9.]+", '') as numeric) -- all other categories do not impact the expense from carrier and are -- excluded else null end ) as total_invoice_amount, approx_count_distinct(tracking_code) as count_tracking_codes, count(*) as count_rows from `dv-vgo-fin-prod.carrier_invoices.easypost_usps_payment_log` group by all order by 1 ``` # To do list _Describe manual actions that need to be done before or after merging (e.g. manual `--full-refresh`, updating Confluence docs, sending out slack comms etc.)._ # Checklist _Fill out only the sections applicable to the PR. prs.description: # Summary [Required] _Describe What & why is being changed. If applicable, how the change was validated & tested. Add links to Jira, RFCs, PRs, Slack, Lucid, etc., if relevant. See GitHub best practices for reference [^1]._ feedback from @Laura-Sn: in invoices we receive from YODEL, there are two ways to identify returns: 1. service_name = 'Return to Sender' (this is not all the cases), 2. looking at events to see if we received a 'return_to_sender' event (this was previously not considered). in this PR, we do the following: * identify returns for YODEL using the tracking event. * if there are duplicates at the tracking code + cost description level, they will be flagged. * the shipment will be compared against the events received for a carrier_leg_id on whether there is a 'return_to_sender' event. * if yes, the identified duplicate invoice row will have it's cost description suffixed with '_return'. * this is such that it will not be flagged as return. the remaining invoice rows which are flagged as duplicates will be 'true' duplicates, which will be escalated with YODEL. **considerations** [1] different lookback period from other joining models (others use 30 days, this has to be longer). in this case, we have to lookback 100 days to more substantially identify 'returns'. looking at historical data, we will get 95% of cases by looking back 98 days based on file upload date. rounded to 100 days. [2] distributions of shipments based on `has_return_event`: only 0.2% of carrier legs are affected, but this will help us to identify 'legitimate' shipments, and claw back returns from those shipments without return events. ```sql select has_return_event, count_carrier_legs, concat( cast( round( count_carrier_legs / sum(count_carrier_legs) over () * 100, 2 ) as string ), "%" ) as perc_carrier_legs from ( select has_return_event, approx_count_distinct(shipment_carrier_leg_id) as count_carrier_legs from `dv-vgo-fin-sb.dev_jeremy_chia.dim_prep_join_invoices_tracking_code_with_returns` group by all ) group by all order by 1 ``` [3] identification of 'legitimate' returns: for 54,024 carrier legs, they were identified as 'legitimate' returns based on the presence of 'return to sender' tracking events. for remaining 45,764 carrier legs, they need to be escalated to YODEL to ask why they are duplicated (no return to sender event). most of the duplicates are in the past months: # To do list _Describe manual actions that need to be done before or after merging (e.g. manual `--full-refresh`, updating Confluence docs, sending out slack comms etc.)._ full refresh of `dim_prep_join_invoices_tracking_code` and `fct_invoice_rows` to remove YODEL rows. include in the full refresh of `dim_prep_join_invoices_tracking_code_with_returns` to add back YODEL rows. ```sh dbt run -s dim_prep_join_invoices_tracking_code dim_prep_join_invoices_tracking_code_with_returns fct_invoice_rows -f ``` # Checklist _Fill out only the sections applicable to the PR. prs.description: # Summary [Required] _Describe What & why is being changed. If applicable, how the change was validated & tested. Add links to Jira, RFCs, PRs, Slack, Lucid, etc., if relevant. See GitHub best practices for reference [^1]._ makes `mart_shipment_legs_invoice_cost_and_revenue` incremental. this is currently the most expensive query which runs in the daily pipeline. the main purpose is to combine estimated costs and actual costs information about shipment legs. the limiting factor here is that actual costs information comes up to several months later after the shipment is created. from historical data, 99.9% of shipments have their first invoice uploaded in 351 days or less. see analysis in https://github.com/vinted/dataverse-vintedgo-dbt/pull/4817. therefore, for the different sources: | source | description | lookback days | |-|-|-| | dim_prep_shipment_legs_information | base information for shipment legs created | 365 days* | | mart_prep_shipment_legs_invoice_rows | actual costs information for shipment legs created, partitioned by shipment_created_at | 365 days* | | mart_prep_shipment_legs_tracking_statuses_finance | tracking events information, determines finance revenue recognition and customer invoice dates. events are always seen after the shipment is created. 99.9% of carrier legs have a shipping event first seen 12 days after creation. see [google colab](https://colab.research.google.com/drive/1mxa2s3xyZzNuE_w5fkLiZdyA6dUjTCx9#scrollTo=YyGxuFS0KwYO). | 365 days* | | fct_carrier_legs_estimated_costs | estimated costs, computed at the same incremental period as dim_prep_shipment_legs_information | 365 days* | | mart_prep_carrier_legs_estimated_costs_on_invoice_weight_v0 | estimated costs, computed at the same incremental period as dim_prep_shipment_legs_information | 365 days* | * 365 days was chosen as the threshold due to the number of days later we expect to be receiving actual costs information. supplementary information: 99.9% files are uploaded for carrier legs within 351 days of the shipment created at dates. for simplicity, we use 365 days as the gauge. this is the biggest prs.description: # Summary [Required] _Describe What & why is being changed. If applicable, how the change was validated & tested. Add links to Jira, RFCs, PRs, Slack, Lucid, etc., if relevant. See GitHub best practices for reference [^1]._ * there are duplicates in `mart_prep_carrier_invoices_shipment_leg_granularity` because each shipment_carrier_leg_id has multiple information, and somehow the window function has returned different results. * move window function out of the incremental model. i tried this variation which seems to work: ```sql with invoice_rows_wide as ( select * except ( first_invoice_id, first_invoice_joining_key, first_invoice_carrier_code, first_invoice_from_country_code, first_invoice_to_country_code, first_invoice_zone, first_invoice_row_number, first_invoice_file_name, first_invoice_date, first_invoice_weight_kg ) from `dv-vgo-fin-prod`.`marts_prep`.`mart_prep_invoice_rows_wide_categories` where shipment_carrier_leg_id is not null and cost_category != "other shipping" -- excluding depo costs for now because of diff currencies from original invoice and shipment_carrier_leg_id in (1677320946, 1663138417) ), add_first_values as ( select shipment_carrier_leg_id, invoice_file_name, invoice_row_number, invoice_cost_description, first_value(invoice_id) over shipment_carrier_leg_window as first_invoice_id, first_value(invoice_joining_key) over shipment_carrier_leg_window as first_invoice_joining_key, -- note that this is only necessary because of DEPO labels that cause -- a single shipment to be able to have two different invoice_carrier_codes first_value(invoice_carrier_code) over shipment_carrier_leg_window as first_invoice_carrier_code, first_value(invoice_from_country_code) over shipment_carrier_leg_window as first_invoice_from_country_code, first_value(invoice_to_country_code) over shipment_carrier_leg_window as first_invoice_to_country_code, first_value(invoice_zone) over shipment_carrier_leg_window as first_invoice_zone, first_value(invoice_row_number) over shipment_carrier_leg_window as first_invoice_row_number, first_value(invoice_file_name) over shipment_carrier_leg_window as first_invoice_file_name, first_value(invoice_date) over shipment_carrier_leg_window as first_invoice_date, first_value(invoice_weight_kg) over shipment_carrier_leg_window as first_invoice_weight_kg from invoice_rows_wide where shipment_carrier_leg_id is not null window shipment_carrier_leg_window as ( partition by shipment_carrier_leg_id # Summary [Required]
_Describe What & why is being changed. If applicable, how the change was validated & tested. Add links to Jira, RFCs, PRs, Slack, Lucid, etc., if relevant.
See GitHub best practices for reference [^1]._

this PR prepares to make `mart_shipment_legs_invoice_cost_and_revenue` incremental:

* by replacing the price list join logic with modular tables.
* subsequent step is to set reading from all component tables as incremental (likely with a look-back period of 180 days).
* the main benefit is that this mart becomes more readable, and what remains here should just be joins between different models.

in addition, because of the changes in columns available, this is similarly adjusted in downstream dependencies.

prs.description: # Summary [Required] * following on from this [RFC](https://vinted.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SA/pages/30268260504/2025-06-05+Optimising+VGo+Finance+s+Costs-Reporting+Models), this is the first step towards making the price-list join logic incremental. * this does the a price list estimation for based on `invoice_weight`, which takes information from a `mart_prep`. **considerations:** why is a longer incremental window needed? * we see that invoices are received up to ~180 days after the shipment was created. * this is to make sure we get the most updated information. ```sql with details as ( select shipment_created_at, invoice_carrier_code, invoice_date, date_diff(shipment_created_at, invoice_date, day) as lookback_days from `dv-vgo-fin-prod.marts.mart_shipment_legs_invoice_cost_and_revenue` where shipment_created_at >= "2025-01-01" ) select lookback_days, count(*) as count_carrier_legs from details group by all order by lookback_days, count_carrier_legs ``` **overview** this is part of a multi-part PR series which will eventually make the models run incrementally. | PR description | link | |-|-| | add incremental models for estimated costs based on backend weights, to result in a new fact for estimated costs | #4711 | | add incremental models for estimated costs based on actual weights (needs to take into account actual cost. this will be implemented as a mart_prep | #4735 | | substitute this in `mart_shipment_legs_invoice_cost_and_revenue`, removing old fields | to be added | | remove fields which are not being used often (for example, arrays which store matches) | to be added | # To do list _Describe manual actions that need to be done before or after merging (e.g. manual `--full-refresh`, updating Confluence docs, sending out slack comms etc.)._ # Checklist _Fill out only the sections applicable to the PR. prs.title: refactor: making price-list join logic incremental (estimated costs)
prs.description:
# Summary [Required]
_Describe What & why is being changed. If applicable, how the change was validated & tested. Add links to Jira, RFCs, PRs, Slack, Lucid, etc., if relevant.
See GitHub best practices for reference [^1]._

* following on from this [RFC](https://vinted.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SA/pages/30268260504/2025-06-05+Optimising+VGo+Finance+s+Costs-Reporting+Models), this is the first step towards making the price-list join logic incremental.
* this starts first with making the price-list join logic, which is based on information which comes from `dim_prep_shipment_legs_information`, incremental.

**considerations:**

why is the model listed as a `_v0`?
* this is because there is expected to be a new price list join logic, following the migration of the price list into the admin tool. see this [confluence page](https://vinted.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/Starship/pages/30001660214/Shipping+pricing+configuration+migration+to+Vinted+Go+Admin+panel#Data-model) for more details. this would effectively be a different version.

why not use `struct`?
* the `struct` is useful for debugging, but has introduced some complexities when new fields are added.
* in addition, it has created more fields in looker, which has caused confusion on which field to use.
* instead, `carrier_contract_price_id` will be used for debugging going forward.

**overview**

this is part of a multi-part PR series which will eventually make the models run incrementally.

| PR description | link |
|-|-|
| add incremental models for estimated costs based on backend weights, to result in a new fact for estimated costs | #4711 | 
| add incremental models for estimated costs based on actual weights (needs to take into account actual cost. this will be implemented as a mart_prep | #4735 |
| substitute this in `mart_shipment_legs_invoice_cost_and_revenue`, removing old fields | to be added |
| remove fields which are not being used often (for example, arrays which store matches) | to be added |

# Summary [Required]
_What & why is being changed. If applicable, how the change was validated & tested. Add links to Jira, PRs, Slack, Lucid, etc., if relevant._

* adding breakdown of the revenue type to the marketplace revenue - at the team's request.

this PR does the following:

* adds accepted values tests on source, to check that all the expected categories are covered.
* adds new columns for the subtypes to marketplace revenue, and all downstream models.

alternatives considered:

* instead of defining the list of subtypes and types in three models, it's possible to define this in the `dbt_project.yml`. i considered this, but noted that because of the migration of shipping pricing models, it might be more intuitive to keep this in the model so there is an awareness of the variables used.

* grouping some of the fields together: for the subtypes, i wanted them to be mutually exclusive and completely exhaustive. i asked if we wanted to group together the subtypes, but the users prefer to keep all of them separate so they have the flexibility to combine the fields as they wish.

prs.description:
# Summary [Required]
_What & why is being changed. If applicable, how the change was validated & tested. Add links to Jira, PRs, Slack, Lucid, etc., if relevant._

to complete the requirement of being able to analyse shipping profit and loss (from a group level), an aggregate mart is needed. this is a follow-up from this PR: https://github.com/vinted/dataverse-marketplace-dbt/pull/8343.

this PR does the following:

1. remove unmatched costs from a granular level. this was a mistake in the previous PR, as the granular level would only have matched costs. this was a mistake.
2. create a `mrt_prep` for actual unmatched costs (from carriers). this is tricky, as we cannot always rely on the carrier's information to derive a route. there will need to be some interrim solution.
3. create a `mrt_prep` for actual no-detail costs (from carriers). will need to make sure the source is tagged with the appropriate access requirements.
4. create an aggregate which things everything together: reporting carrier, reporting from/to, invoice month (takes invoice issued to marketplace user's month)

note: this makes use of a new model created in https://github.com/vinted/dataverse-vintedgo-dbt/pull/4483/.
