prs.title: feat: revise usps shipment invoice - takes only positive values from adjustments
prs.description: # Summary [Required] _What & why is being changed. If applicable, how the change was validated & tested. Add links to Jira, PRs, Slack, Lucid, etc., if relevant._ >[!WARNING] > do not merge during week of 02.09 - 06.09 (month-end closing) * from USPS shipment invoice information, only positive values from the adjustments should be taken into account. * negative adjustment amounts are considered in the shipments table, as with the base rate. >[!NOTE] > more information on the expected changes available in [google sheets](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1pyJ2oY3vKyhqdNq3f7ueQidQKXw9EenOl04GT12u_vA/edit?gid=1460442205#gid=1460442205) because a bulk of the 'base costs' (which were potentially being double-counted previously) are being removed, there are significant decreases in the amounts: ```sql with shipment_invoice_new_logic as ( select label_date, invoice_currency, sum(invoice_amount) as new_logic_invoice_amount from `dv-vgo-fin-sb.dev_jeremy_chia.stg_carrier_invoices__easypost_usps_shipment_invoice_table_v2` group by all ), shipment_invoice_current_logic as ( select label_date, invoice_currency, sum(invoice_amount) as current_logic_invoice_amount from `dv-vgo-fin-prod.staging.stg_carrier_invoices__easypost_usps_shipment_invoice` group by all ) select *, new_logic_invoice_amount - current_logic_invoice_amount as difference from shipment_invoice_new_logic full join shipment_invoice_current_logic using (label_date, invoice_currency) where new_logic_invoice_amount - current_logic_invoice_amount != 0 order by label_date desc ``` # To do list _If applicable, manual actions that need to be done before or after merging (e.g. manual `--full-refresh`)._ # Checklist _Fill out only the sections applicable to the PR.     * You are either creating from scratch or adding to an existing ETL infrastructure of related objects.

    * Any outer joins.

    * etc.

    1. If the change is a revert, start the commit message with the word “revert” and use the same commit messages as used for the original commit.

    * You are either creating from scratch or adding to an existing ETL infrastructure of related objects.
    * You are adding a new calculation, and you would like to explain the motivation for calculating it your way.
    * You are fixing something done previously, and you want to reference the mistake.

    * Any filters with specific values.
    * Any hardcoded values.
    * Any outer joins.
    * Creating a `val` that helps with complex transformations (see code example below).
    * etc.

this PR will:

* implement the DAG configurations proposed in the document
* combine several steps in the DAG to reduce latency

what are the main changes?

| dag name | description | cron (UTC) |
|-|-|-|
| vgo_finance_dag  | this is the original dag, which will build with only the required tests (checks for model join keys). all other auxiliary tests will be excluded for the main build. fulfilment of SLA will depend on this. it is expected that the daily pipeline will run faster. (the tests are taken out of this DAG) | 10 5 * * * |
| vgo_finance_test_highfreq_lowimpact_dag | this contains tests to check on the data quality; for example, the shipment join failures, price list join failures, accepted values tests. this will run independently of the main pipeline. | 0 7 * * * |
| vgo_finance_test_highfreq_highimpact_dag | these are tests on primarily inputs coming from google sheets. designed to alert more frequently when there are errors. | 0 9,11,14 * * * |
| vgo_finance_source_tester_dag | this is a test on recently uploaded invoices to give quick feedback on the most recently uploaded invoices. | (every 10 minutes) |

Everything makes sense to me. Just one thing, most of the _eur suffix descriptions say that its converted to EURs using the average rate of the invoice month, while its not necessarily true, I just realised:
```
coalesce(
                    unioned_carrier_invoices.label_date, unioned_carrier_invoices.invoice_date
                )
```
label_date is prioritised in the join, also its not always equal to invoice month. 

Something to keep in mind, maybe to fix later

prs.title: feat: for available for pick-up shipments and delivered shipments, populate customer invoice date
prs.description:
# Summary [Required]
_What & why is being changed. If applicable, how the change was validated & tested. Add links to Jira, PRs, Slack, Lucid, etc., if relevant._

see [FDSA-182](https://vinted.atlassian.net/browse/FDSA-182) for more information.

* we found missing costs for POPO. these refer to transactions in the marketplace for which a shipping revenue was recorded but no corresponding costs. 
* when investigating, we found that it was an issue with the data model. some shipments were being filtered out because it had a null customer invoice date.
* the reason why the customer invoice date was null was because there were no pre-delivery events recorded from the carrier. we can however see an event for delivery.

for shipments which are delivered, we therefore want to make sure they are invoiced. therefore this PR changes the logic for which the customer invoice date is being populated:

> By default, take the first seen shipping indicating events as the customer invoice date.
>
> However, if there are no such events, the following will take precedence:
> * If the shipment has an available for pick up date, the customer invoice date will be this date.
> * Otherwise, if the shipment does not have this, the customer invoice date will be the delivered date.
>
> If there are no events at all, there will be no customer invoice date.

in addition, for visibility, i am adding two flags to track how the revenue recognition date and customer invoice date will be populated so that we can monitor the data quality.

prs.title: fix: change carrier invoices staging layer back to views
prs.description:
# Summary [Required]
_What & why is being changed. If applicable, how the change was validated & tested. Add links to Jira, PRs, Slack, Lucid, etc., if relevant._

* in  #2024, the materialisation of all staging layers was changed to a table.
* this caused the source_not_null_* tests ([VGOFIN-407](https://vinted.atlassian.net/browse/VGOFIN-407)) to not function as intended - because the filter time frame is at 10 minute intervals, whereas the staging layer only gets refreshed daily.
* to allow these tests to run as intended, the materialisation should be changed back to a view. this is at the tradeoff for the model being called multiple times.
* concurrently, the missing tests should be backfilled as in [VGOFIN-416](https://vinted.atlassian.net/browse/VGOFIN-416).

prs.title: fix: backfill union all test missing data since 2024-07-09
prs.description:
# Summary [Required]
_What & why is being changed. If applicable, how the change was validated & tested. Add links to Jira, PRs, Slack, Lucid, etc., if relevant._

context:
* a summary of test failures are stored in a [google sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1oyCZ5-fxbITsN380WdCPjcNNH7XdEl2WH6uJ_Jl4qHE), and posted to [#vgo-carrier-invoice-upload-function](https://vinted.slack.com/archives/C06105W2T6F).
* there were no new entries from 2024-07-09. the issue is discussed and documented in [VGOFIN-407](https://vinted.atlassian.net/browse/VGOFIN-407).
* the issue is because the staging layers have now been materialised as tables, and repeatedly running the logic on what was previously views has become more and more costly and expensive.
* previously, when it was materialised as views, it was possible to run the test to get the result.

remedy:
* a notebook has been created to populate the results from the last effective run: [google colab](https://colab.research.google.com/drive/1OUFVwmqKRnfpC5oFvkS_zL_hyARdHq5W#scrollTo=NGdtd10meZpJ).
* the results of this run are stored in `dv-vgo-fin-sb.test_failures._union_all_test_failures_tmp`.

this PR:
* creates a custom query to union the results from the aforementioned table and the live table to backfill the results.

```sh
compiled Code at target/run/vgo_finance/models/marts_prep/mart_prep_shipment_legs_invoice_cost_and_revenue.sql
```

prs.title: feat: update historical snapshot to be taken on the first day of the month
prs.description:
# Summary [Required]
_What & why is being changed. If applicable, how the change was validated & tested. Add links to Jira, PRs, Slack, Lucid, etc., if relevant._

historical snapshots were created to give a view of what the underlying data was when it was reported at that point in time. these were created in:

| for | PR |
|-|-|
| customer invoices & revenue recognition | #1507 |
| price lists | #2108 |

this PR makes changes to **when the snapshot is taken**:
* this was previously done on the second day of the month.
* to reflect when the reports are generated (the first day of the month), the snapshot shall be changed to be taken on the first day of the month.

in addition, the airflow variable `data_interval_end` will be used instead:
* it was noticed that `execution_date` lags by one day - for runs on "2024-07-26", the value is "2024-07-25".
* therefore, to correct this such that it will be taken on the first day of the month.

# To do list

prs.description:
# Summary [Required]
_What & why is being changed. If applicable, how the change was validated & tested. Add links to Jira, PRs, Slack, Lucid, etc., if relevant._

* in difference analysis, we have discovered that 75% of changes post-period in 2024-04 come from price list changes ([jira comment](https://vinted.atlassian.net/browse/VGOFIN-157?focusedCommentId=719242)).
* currently, there is no way to determine what the change in the price list is, as we do not have a historical view of what the price list looked like at any point in time.

this PR:

* creates a historic table which takes snapshots of the price list together with the snapshots for customer invoices and revenue recognition.

incidental to this change, this PR also:

* does explicit naming of columns in `dim_carrier_contract_prices`
* includes a column for `shipment_sale_rate_markup_coeff` in `dim_carrier_contract_prices` to make more obvious what rows had mark-up applied, and which ones did not.

# Summary [Required]
_What & why is being changed. If applicable, how the change was validated & tested. Add links to Jira, PRs, Slack, Lucid, etc., if relevant._

>[!warning]
> there are several fields which are not immediately available in `fct_{status}_carrier_legs` which needs to be added. this is addressed in https://github.com/vinted/dataverse-vintedgo-dbt/pull/2124.

* shipment carriers has been remodelled https://github.com/vinted/dataverse-vintedgo-dbt/pull/1623.
* `dim_shipment_configuration`, which captures all information achieved by joining various dimensions previously was implemented here: https://github.com/vinted/dataverse-vintedgo-dbt/pull/1172

* this PR replaces the dependencies in `mart_prep_shipment_legs_invoice_cost_and_revenue ` with the new tables.

## Mapping of current column names to new sources

the main CTE where joins are being done is `shipment_legs_add_extra_columns`. the table below summarises the source of columns, which takes information from only two (2) sets of tables (previously six (6)) - `dim_shipment_configuration` and `fct_{status}_carrier_legs`. 

| column name | new source | new source column name | remarks |
|-|-|-|-|
| `shipment_carrier_leg_id` | `fct_{status}_carrier_legs` |  `carrier_leg_id` | |
| `carrier_parcel_type_id` |  `dim_shipment_configuration` | `carrier_parcel_type_id`| |
| `shipment_created_at` | `fct_{status}_carrier_legs` |  `carrier_leg_created_at` | |
| `carrier_service_id` | `dim_shipment_configuration` | `carrier_service_id` | |
| `integration_name` | `fct_{status}_carrier_legs` | `carrier_leg_integration_name` | |
|  `selling_price_currency` | `fct_{status}_carrier_legs` | `parent_shipment_selling_price_currency ` | added in #2124 |
| `shipment_order_status` | `fct_{status}_carrier_legs` | `parent_shipment_processing_status` | |
| `carrier_code` | `fct_{status}_carrier_legs` | `carrier_code` | |
| `carrier_id_first_mile_backend` |  `dim_shipment_configuration` | `carrier_id_first_mile_backend` | |
| `carrier_id_last_mile_backend` | `dim_shipment_configuration` | `carrier_id_last_mile_backend` | |
| `shipment_leg_from_country_code` | `dim_shipment_configuration` | `country_code_origin` | |
| `shipment_leg_to_country_code` | `dim_shipment_configuration` | `country_code_destination`| |
| `shipment_min_weight_kg` | `dim_shipment_configuration` | `parcel_min_mass_kg` | |
| `shipment_max_weight_kg` | `dim_shipment_configuration` | `parcel_max_mass_kg` | |
| `carrier_id_first_mile` | `dim_shipment_configuration` | `carrier_id_first_mile` | |
| `carrier_id_last_mile` | `dim_shipment_configuration` | `carrier_id_last_mile` | |
| `is_hvf_shipment_leg` | `dim_shipment_configuration` (derivation of) | `has_item_verification` | |
| `number_in_route` | `fct_{status}_carrier_legs` | `carrier_leg_number_in_route` | |
| `is_first_leg_multi_leg_shipment` | `fct_{status}_carrier_legs` (derivation of) | `carrier_leg_number_in_route` | | 
| `is_second_leg_multi_leg_shipment` | `fct_{status}_carrier_legs` (derivation of) | `carrier_leg_number_in_route` | |
| `service_type_name_price_list` | `dim_shipment_configuration` | `delivery_type_code` | join with seeds `dim_delivery_types` |
| `shipment_id` | `fct_{status}_carrier_legs` | `shipment_id` | |
| `customer_id` | `dim_shipment_configuration` | `customer_id` | |
| `delivery_type_code` | `dim_shipment_configuration` | `delivery_type_code` | |
| `reference_code` | `fct_{status}_carrier_legs` | `reference_code` | |



the join key between `dim_shipment_configuration` and `fct_{status}_carrier_legs` is `parcel_configuration_key`.

prs.description:
# Summary [Required]
_What & why is being changed. If applicable, how the change was validated & tested. Add links to Jira, PRs, Slack, Lucid, etc., if relevant._

* shipment carriers has been remodelled https://github.com/vinted/dataverse-vintedgo-dbt/pull/1623.
* this PR replaces the dependencies in `dim_prep_shipment_carrier_legs_joining_keys` with the new tables.

* in addition, `shipment_carrier_leg_id` and `shipment_tracking_code` have a 1:1 relationship. see set-up in [`int_carrier_legs_prep`](https://github.com/vinted/dataverse-vintedgo-dbt/blob/VGOFIN-326-replace-dependencies-in-dim-prep-shipment-carrier-legs-joining-keys/vgo_general/models/dimensional_prep/int_carrier_legs_prep/int_carrier_legs_prep.sql#L65)
* this is also tested. there are no cases where there is more than one tracking code per shipment carrier leg.
```sql
select *
from `dv-vgo-fin-prod.dim_prep.dim_prep_shipment_carrier_legs_joining_keys`
where
    timestamp_trunc(shipment_created_at, month) > timestamp("2024-01-01")
    and array_length(shipment_tracking_codes) > 1
```
* therefore, in this PR, i also propose to undo the array agg for shipment tracking codes.

# To do list
_If applicable, manual actions that need to be done before or after merging (e.g. manual `--full-refresh`)._

- [x] create samples
```sh
dbt run-operation create_sample --args '{source: fct_processed_carrier_legs, prod_bq_project: dv-vgo-gen-prod}' --target dev_samples
dbt run-operation create_sample --args '{source: fct_failed_carrier_legs, prod_bq_project: dv-vgo-gen-prod}' --target dev_samples
dbt run-operation create_sample --args '{source: fct_cancelled_carrier_legs, prod_bq_project: dv-vgo-gen-prod}' --target dev_samples
dbt run-operation create_sample --args '{source: fct_processed_carrier_legs, prod_bq_project: dv-vgo-gen-prod}' --target test_samples
dbt run-operation create_sample --args '{source: fct_failed_carrier_legs, prod_bq_project: dv-vgo-gen-prod}' --target test_samples
dbt run-operation create_sample --args '{source: fct_cancelled_carrier_legs, prod_bq_project: dv-vgo-gen-prod}' --target test_samples
```

- [ ] test results of joins with the new table source:
```sql
with
    union_shipment_legs as (
        -- processed legs
        select
            carrier_leg_id,
            carrier_code,
            carrier_leg_external_code,
            shipment_id,
            reference_code,
            carrier_leg_account_code,
            carrier_leg_barcode,
            carrier_leg_tracking_code,
            carrier_leg_created_at,
            parent_shipment_processing_status
        from `dv-vgo-gen-prod`.`facts`.`fct_processed_carrier_legs`
        where
            date(carrier_leg_created_at) in (
                "2024-03-14",
                "2024-03-15",
                "2024-03-16",
                "2024-03-17",
                "2024-03-18",
                "2024-03-19",
                "2024-03-20"
            )
        union all
        -- failed legs
        select
            carrier_leg_id,
            carrier_code,
            carrier_leg_external_code,
            shipment_id,
            reference_code,
            carrier_leg_account_code,
            carrier_leg_barcode,
            carrier_leg_tracking_code,
            carrier_leg_created_at,
            parent_shipment_processing_status
        from `dv-vgo-gen-prod`.`facts`.`fct_failed_carrier_legs`
        where
            date(carrier_leg_created_at) in (
                "2024-03-14",
                "2024-03-15",
                "2024-03-16",
                "2024-03-17",
                "2024-03-18",
                "2024-03-19",
                "2024-03-20"
            )
        union all
        -- canceled legs
        select
            carrier_leg_id,
            carrier_code,
            carrier_leg_external_code,
            shipment_id,
            reference_code,
            carrier_leg_account_code,
            carrier_leg_barcode,
            carrier_leg_tracking_code,
            carrier_leg_created_at,
            parent_shipment_processing_status
        from `dv-vgo-gen-prod`.`facts`.`fct_cancelled_carrier_legs`
        where
            date(carrier_leg_created_at) in (
                "2024-03-14",
                "2024-03-15",
                "2024-03-16",
                "2024-03-17",
                "2024-03-18",
                "2024-03-19",
                "2024-03-20"
            )
    ),

    renamed_shipment_legs as (
        select
            carrier_leg_id as shipment_carrier_leg_id,
            carrier_code,
            carrier_leg_external_code as external_shipment_code,
            shipment_id,
            reference_code as shipment_reference_code,
            carrier_leg_account_code as shipment_account_code,
            carrier_leg_barcode as shipment_barcode,
            carrier_leg_tracking_code as shipment_tracking_code,
            carrier_leg_created_at as shipment_created_at,
            parent_shipment_processing_status as shipment_order_status
        from union_shipment_legs
    ),

    carrier_codes as (
        select backend_carrier_code, invoice_carrier_code
        from `dv-vgo-fin-sb`.`dev_jeremy_chia`.`carrier_codes`
    ),

    joining_keys as (
        select
            renamed_shipment_legs.shipment_carrier_leg_id,
            renamed_shipment_legs.external_shipment_code,
            renamed_shipment_legs.shipment_reference_code,
            renamed_shipment_legs.shipment_account_code,
            renamed_shipment_legs.shipment_barcode,
            renamed_shipment_legs.shipment_created_at,
            renamed_shipment_legs.shipment_order_status,
            renamed_shipment_legs.carrier_code,
            array_agg(
                distinct
                case
                    when carrier_codes.invoice_carrier_code is not null
                    then carrier_codes.invoice_carrier_code
                    else "unknown"
                end
            ) as invoice_carrier_codes,
            case
                when renamed_shipment_legs.shipment_tracking_code is not null
                then renamed_shipment_legs.shipment_tracking_code
                else "unknown"
            end as shipment_tracking_code
        from renamed_shipment_legs
        left join
            carrier_codes
            on renamed_shipment_legs.carrier_code = carrier_codes.backend_carrier_code
        group by all
    )

select *
from joining_keys
```

prs.title: feat: expose new column (tracking code) from USPS payment logs
prs.description: # Summary [Required] _What & why is being changed. If applicable, how the change was validated & tested. Add links to Jira, PRs, Slack, Lucid, etc., if relevant._ broader context: * there are many unmatched USPS shipments. this is primarily because the payment log files did not have a tracking code. * we want to see `tracking_code` as part of the payment log. when downloading this information from the USPS portal directly, it is possible to see this column. it is however excluded from downloaded prs.title: feat: preferential join for account_code with IT for inpost IT invoices
prs.description:
# Summary [Required]
_What & why is being changed. If applicable, how the change was validated & tested. Add links to Jira, PRs, Slack, Lucid, etc., if relevant._

* there was 2.1m EUR of tracking codes flagged as duplicates from mondial.
* after investigation, we found that the mondial lines were more likely joined to the correct shipment_carrier_leg_id. instead it was the inpost IT lines where the joins originally were first made which might have been inaccurate.
* this is because, for example, for the `shipment_tracking_code = '12657510'`, there are multiple account codes.
* feedback from mondial indicates that joins should be to the `shipment_number`, which has a two-letter prefix and the tracking code. this is not available in our backend shipment keys table.
* the next best alternative is to prioritise the join where the `shipment_account_code` starts with `IT` for inpost IT invoices.
* a new `dim_prep_join_invoices` is created to deal with this case.

prs.description:
# Summary [Required]
_What & why is being changed. If applicable, how the change was validated & tested. Add links to Jira, PRs, Slack, Lucid, etc., if relevant._

* arising from [2024-07-11's pipeline failure](https://vinted.slack.com/archives/C041KP1LXGS/p1720677338669009)
* when looking into it, appears at the row in concern is a total row:

compared:
totals of all the other rows
```sql
select sum(cast(gross_amount as float64)), sum(cast(fuel_surcharge as float64))
from `dv-vgo-fin-prod.carrier_invoices.postnord_se`
where
    _file_name
    = 'gs://dv-vgo-fin-prod-csv-cleaner-output-bucket/postnord_se/logic_v1/file_upload_date=2024-07-10/schema=e838a0ebb8/902881373028 del 1 till kund.parquet'
    and row_number != 603005
```
and the offending row
```sql
select sum(cast(gross_amount as float64)), sum(cast(fuel_surcharge as float64))
from `dv-vgo-fin-prod.carrier_invoices.postnord_se`
where
    _file_name
    = 'gs://dv-vgo-fin-prod-csv-cleaner-output-bucket/postnord_se/logic_v1/file_upload_date=2024-07-10/schema=e838a0ebb8/902881373028 del 1 till kund.parquet'
    and row_number = 603005
```

resolution:
* what can be identified is that this looks like a total row.
* these total rows can be seen if `item_id` and `service_name` are empty.
* therefore, they should be filtered out.

prs.title: feat: reduce CI runtime - use `tablesample system` and `rand` to reduce sample size at source for `vgo_finance`
prs.description:
# Summary [Required]
_What & why is being changed. If applicable, how the change was validated & tested. Add links to Jira, PRs, Slack, Lucid, etc., if relevant._

> [!NOTE]
> refactored in https://github.com/vinted/dataverse-vintedgo-dbt/pull/2035 - uses a macro instead of redefinition.

context:
* testing costs for `dv-vgo-fin-test` are significant. in the last 60 days, these form 1/6 of the total costs for `dv-vgo-fin` (source: [looker explore](https://looker.vinted.net/explore/billing_bigquery/bigquery_job_costs?qid=9wXH94LCq3VdlAK7UGod8j&origin_space=3253&toggle=vis)). as the data grows, this will only become more and more.
* CI time for `vgo_finance`'s build is getting longer (at approx. 7m30s~) due to the growing size of data and more models. poorer developer experience as CI takes longer to merge.

this PR does the following:
* where `target='test'`, limits the amount of rows which are being read from source is lesser. this is achieved using the following:

    * where possible, `testsample system (1 percent)` is being used. this is because from a bigquery point-of-view, less data is being queried (i.e. we are billed less). see [documentation](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/table-sampling). there are limitations to this approach. for example, in models where `get_most_common_month()` is called, this did not work as it returned an error: _Possible reasons: (1) sampled table referenced more than once or (2) sampling used inside IN subquery._ (see [error](https://github.com/vinted/dataverse-vintedgo-dbt/actions/runs/9839036393/job/27160295201))

    * otherwise, `where rand() < 0.01` will be used to reduce the sample size. unfortunately in this case, the whole of the original table is still being read.

* materialised the staging layers where base data is being read in AND heavy transformations are being run as tables. this is more efficient from a compute point of view. _why? because in downstream applications from the staging layer (tests, dim_joining_key, etc.), if it is materialised as a view, the same query is being executed multiple times - one time for each downstream application of it. this is not ideal and also increases compute time. materialising this as a table saves compute cost and the volume of data being read._

* changed samples configuration (see [confluence](https://vinted.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DPV2/pages/28456748297/Creating+dev+and+test+samples+guide)) to do non-deterministic random sampling. this is in the event that sample creation is automated.

results:
| commit | dbt build timing |
|-|-|
| [1c203e1](https://github.com/vinted/dataverse-vintedgo-dbt/actions/runs/9841160642/job/27167246462) (before change implemented) | 7m39s |

| [c0b2bcb](https://github.com/vinted/dataverse-vintedgo-dbt/actions/runs/9841949241/job/27169858588) | 4m0s |
| [43cc14a](https://github.com/vinted/dataverse-vintedgo-dbt/actions/runs/9842175730/job/27170614877) | 3m59s |


references:
* [Sampling data with dbt and BigQuery: a strategy to reduce costs](https://medium.com/indiciumtech/sampling-data-with-dbt-and-bigquery-a-strategy-to-reduce-costs-ef059b9e2144)
* [29 Ways to Reduce Costs in Data Pipelines, Workflows & Analyses](https://www.getdbt.com/resources/guides/29-ways-to-reduce-costs-in-data-pipelines-workflows-and-analyses)

* also standardises the names used using the constructor with manual adjustments:

```python
def capitalise_first_letter(word):
  return word[0].upper() + word[1:]

def handle_explicit_scopes(dimension_name, aggregation):
  # e.g. matching_prices_backend_weight.price_list_max_weight_kg
  # gives: matching_prices_backend_weight.sum_price_list_max_weight_kg
  if '.' in dimension_name:
    explicit_scope = dimension_name.split('.')[0]
    field_name = dimension_name.split('.')[1]
    return f"{explicit_scope}.{aggregation}_{field_name}"
  else:
    return f"{aggregation}_{dimension_name}"

def construct_measure(dimension, aggregation):
  measure = {
    'type': aggregation,
    'sql': "${"+dimension['name']+"}",
    'description': f"{capitalise_first_letter(aggregation)} of {dimension['description']}",
    'group_label': dimension['group_label'] if 'group_label' in dimension.keys() else '',
    'name': f"{handle_explicit_scopes(dimension['name'], aggregation)}",
    'value_format_name': 'decimal_2',
    'tags': ["custom_content"]
  }

  return measure
```

prs.title: fix: clean column names
prs.description:
the balance statement ([example](https://console.cloud.google.com/storage/browser/dv-vgo-fin-prod-datasets/checkout/report_name%3Dbalance_statement/entity_id%3Dent_kvzvnposwjiu7dahvcmnncs7o4/dt%3D2024-06-12/file_name%3Dstatement_ent_kvzvnposwjiu7dahvcmnncs7o4_20240612_20240612?pageState=(%22StorageObjectListTable%22:(%22f%22:%22%255B%255D%22))&authuser=0&project=dv-vgo-fin-prod)) as illegal characters which prevent external sources from being staged.

the offending column is `ï»¿Report ID` and it shall be parsed to `report_id`.

> [!NOTE]
> will need to deploy new release after this is enabled

to test the changes which are being made, use:

```python
import re
def _clean_column_names(columns: list) -> list:
    """
    Cleans column names by replacing spaces with underscores, removing illegal characters,
    and converting to lowercase.

    For example, in the balance statement report, there was a column "ï»¿Report ID".
    This needs to be cleaned to "report_id".

    Args:
        columns (list of str): The list of column names to be cleaned.

    Returns:
        list of str: The cleaned list of column names.
    """
    columns = [col.replace(" ", "_") for col in columns]
    columns = [re.sub(r"[^\w]", "", col) for col in columns]
    columns = [col.lower() for col in columns]
    columns = [col.encode('ascii', 'ignore').decode('ascii') for col in columns]
    return columns

lst = ["ï»¿Report ID","Entity ID"]
_clean_column_names(lst)
```

prs.title: fix: accommodate balance statement file formats
prs.description:
main change:
* adding `_find_file_date_ending(file_name)` to handle different filename formats.

why:
* balance statement pipeline was failing because of this error:
```sh
[2024-06-13, 05:02:30 UTC] {pod_manager.py:435} INFO - [base] ERROR:root:file name statement_ent_kvzvnposwjiu7dahvcmnncs7o4_20240612_20240612.csv does not follow usual format
```

* this caused the subsequent error because the regex expression did not pick anything up, and therefore this error was thrown:
```sh
[2024-06-13, 05:02:30 UTC] {pod_manager.py:435} INFO - [base] Traceback (most recent call last):
[2024-06-13, 05:02:30 UTC] {pod_manager.py:435} INFO - [base]   File "<frozen runpy>", line 198, in _run_module_as_main
[2024-06-13, 05:02:30 UTC] {pod_manager.py:435} INFO - [base]   File "<frozen runpy>", line 88, in _run_code
[2024-06-13, 05:02:30 UTC] {pod_manager.py:435} INFO - [base]   File "/src/main.py", line 62, in <module>
[2024-06-13, 05:02:30 UTC] {pod_manager.py:435} INFO - [base]     run()
[2024-06-13, 05:02:30 UTC] {pod_manager.py:435} INFO - [base]   File "/src/main.py", line 43, in run
[2024-06-13, 05:02:30 UTC] {pod_manager.py:435} INFO - [base]     download_and_load_reports(
[2024-06-13, 05:02:30 UTC] {pod_manager.py:435} INFO - [base]   File "/src/utils.py", line 38, in download_and_load_reports
[2024-06-13, 05:02:30 UTC] {pod_manager.py:435} INFO - [base]     download_reports(report_list, entity_id, api_key, bucket, lines_per_file)
[2024-06-13, 05:02:30 UTC] {pod_manager.py:435} INFO - [base]   File "/src/utils.py", line 116, in download_reports
[2024-06-13, 05:02:30 UTC] {pod_manager.py:435} INFO - [base]     file_date = f"{file_date_ending[0][1:5]}-{file_date_ending[0][5:7]}-{file_date_ending[0][7:9]}"
[2024-06-13, 05:02:30 UTC] {pod_manager.py:435} INFO - [base]                    ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^
[2024-06-13, 05:02:31 UTC] {pod_manager.py:448} INFO - [base] IndexError: list index out of range
```

* the file format it expects was:
```python
filename = 'financial-actions_ent_kvzvnposwjiu7dahvcmnncs7o4_20240614_20240615_1.csv'
```

* but for balance statement (for now, we only know this applies specifically to balance statements), the file format is:
```python
filename = 'statement_ent_kvzvnposwjiu7dahvcmnncs7o4_20240615_20240615.csv'
```

* therefore, the regex was revised to accommodate different variations. this is reflected in the function `_find_file_date_ending`.
* see this [google colab](https://api-reference.checkout.com/#tag/Reports) (access required) - it was tested to work here.


other incidental changes:
* linting from black.


prs.title: feat: add illegitimate cost measures to cost and revenue table
prs.description:
* adds illegitimate cost measures to cost and revenue table
* also standardises the names used using the constructor with manual adjustments:

```python
def capitalise_first_letter(word):
  return word[0].upper() + word[1:]

def handle_explicit_scopes(dimension_name, aggregation):
  # e.g. matching_prices_backend_weight.price_list_max_weight_kg
  # gives: matching_prices_backend_weight.sum_price_list_max_weight_kg
  if '.' in dimension_name:
    explicit_scope = dimension_name.split('.')[0]
    field_name = dimension_name.split('.')[1]
    return f"{explicit_scope}.{aggregation}_{field_name}"
  else:
    return f"{aggregation}_{dimension_name}"

def construct_measure(dimension, aggregation):
  measure = {
    'type': aggregation,
    'sql': "${"+dimension['name']+"}",
    'description': f"{capitalise_first_letter(aggregation)} of {dimension['description']}",
    'group_label': dimension['group_label'] if 'group_label' in dimension.keys() else '',
    'name': f"{handle_explicit_scopes(dimension['name'], aggregation)}",
    'value_format_name': 'decimal_2',
    'tags': ["custom_content"]
  }

  return measure
```

prs.description:
# Summary [Required]
_What & why is being changed. If applicable, how the change was validated & tested. Add links to Jira, PRs, Slack, Lucid, etc., if relevant._

* fixes schema mismatch - see [error](https://github.com/vinted/dataverse-vintedgo-looker/actions/runs/9478411315/job/26114806576):

```sh
Schema Mismatch for model mart_historic_shipment_legs_revenue_recognition!!
            BigQuery refers to the model generated from running the dbt model (i.e. the SQL file.)
            dbt (or dbt Manifest) here refers to the columns named in the YAML file.
            There seems to be a mismatch between the schemas for these (BigQuery and dbt)
            Columns found in BigQuery not present in dbt:  matching_prices_backend_weight_v2.shipment_base_rate_from_carrier_excl_vat,matching_prices_backend_weight.to_zone_price_list,fallback_prices_excl_vat_backend_weight.shipment_purchase_rate_from_carrier_excl_vat,matching_prices_backend_weight.shipment_purchase_rate_from_carrier_excl_vat,matching_prices_backend_weight.shipment_sale_rate_excl_vat,matching_prices_backend_weight_v2.to_zone_price_list,matching_prices_invoice_weight_v2.price_list_min_weight_kg,matching_prices_backend_weight.price_list_min_weight_kg,matching_prices_backend_weight.from_zone_price_list,matching_prices_invoice_weight_v2.shipment_base_rate_from_carrier_excl_vat,matching_prices_invoice_weight_v2.price_list_max_weight_kg,matching_prices_invoice_weight_v2,matching_prices_backend_weight_v2,matching_prices_invoice_weight.price_list_min_weight_kg,matching_prices_invoice_weight_v2.to_zone_price_list,matching_prices_invoice_weight.from_zone_price_list,matching_prices_invoice_weight_v2.shipment_purchase_rate_from_carrier_excl_vat,matching_prices_invoice_weight.price_list_max_weight_kg,matching_prices_backend_weight_v2.shipment_purchase_rate_from_carrier_excl_vat,matching_prices_backend_weight_v2.from_zone_price_list,fallback_prices_excl_vat_backend_weight.shipment_base_rate_from_carrier_excl_vat,matching_prices_invoice_weight_v2.from_zone_price_list,fallback_prices_excl_vat_invoice_weight.shipment_purchase_rate_from_carrier_excl_vat,matching_prices_invoice_weight.shipment_purchase_rate_from_carrier_excl_vat,matching_prices_backend_weight_v2.price_list_max_weight_kg,matching_prices_invoice_weight.to_zone_price_list,matching_prices_backend_weight_v2.price_list_min_weight_kg,fallback_prices_excl_vat_invoice_weight.shipment_base_rate_from_carrier_excl_vat,matching_prices_backend_weight.price_list_max_weight_kg,matching_prices_backend_weight_v2.shipment_sale_rate_excl_vat
            Columns present in DBT not found in BigQuery: has_fallback_price_from_pricelist,fallback_shipment_sale_rates_excl_vat
```

* because the data structure of some fields were changed, there's a v2. all fields (v1, v2) are hidden, and they should be coalesced in looker if needed.

general constructor (some manual changes were still made to map the fields to the right description):

more information in this [notebook](https://colab.research.google.com/drive/1D88VdOUpSrvSpgZatUENyCZg7IvcQoZ4?authuser=1#scrollTo=Ylwy2GwdoUdH) (request accesss)
```python
def _capitalise_first_letter(word):
  return word[0].upper() + word[1:]

def _parse_group_label(field_scope):
  field_scope_lst = field_scope.split('_')
  return ' '.join([_capitalise_first_letter(word) for word in field_scope_lst])

def construct_column(field):
  # explicit scopes
  if '.' in field:
    field_lst = field.split('.')
    doc_field = field_lst[1]
  else:
    field_lst = [field]
    doc_field = field

  return {
      'name': field,
      'description':  '{{ doc(' + doc_field + ') }}',
      'meta': {
          'group_label': _parse_group_label(field_lst[0])
      }
  }

```

prs.title: feat: add measures for new dimensions in mart_carrier_invoices_totals
prs.description:
* from https://github.com/vinted/dataverse-vintedgo-dbt/pull/1866, new dimensions were added
* they were created and merged in https://github.com/vinted/dataverse-vintedgo-looker/pull/426
* this PR adds the corresponding measures

uses the constructor in this [google colab](https://colab.research.google.com/drive/1bGO8AJI1nJ8OdN3U-z53NuzZ3i53AJGw?authuser=1#scrollTo=nyjjMyJf6xAT) (request access):
```python
def capitalise_first_letter(word):
  return word[0].upper() + word[1:]

def handle_explicit_scopes(dimension_name, aggregation):
  # e.g. matching_prices_backend_weight.price_list_max_weight_kg
  # gives: matching_prices_backend_weight.sum_price_list_max_weight_kg
  if '.' in dimension_name:
    explicit_scope = dimension_name.split('.')[0]
    field_name = dimension_name.split('.')[1]
    return f"{explicit_scope}.{aggregation}_{field_name}"
  else:
    return f"{aggregation}_{dimension_name}"

def construct_measure(dimension, aggregation):
  measure = {
    'type': aggregation,
    'sql': "${"+dimension['name']+"}",
    'description': f"{capitalise_first_letter(aggregation)} of {dimension['description']}",
    'group_label': dimension['group_label'] if 'group_label' in dimension.keys() else '',
    'name': f"{handle_explicit_scopes(dimension['name'], aggregation)}",
    'value_format_name': 'decimal_2',
    'tags': ["custom_content"]
  }

  return measure
```

this is the main construction:

```python
def capitalise_first_letter(word):
  return word[0].upper() + word[1:]

def construct_measure(dimension, aggregation):
  measure = {
    'type': aggregation,
    'sql': "${"+dimension['name']+"}",
    'description': f"{capitalise_first_letter(aggregation)} of {dimension['description']}",
    'group_label': dimension['group_label'],
    'name': f"{aggregation}_{dimension['name']}",
    'tags': ["custom_content"]
  }

  return measure

measures = []

for dimension in lookml_json['views'][0]['dimensions']:
  if '_id' in dimension['name']:
    dimension['type'] = 'string'
  elif dimension['type'] == 'number':
    measures.append(construct_measure(dimension, 'sum'))
    measures.append(construct_measure(dimension, 'average'))
    dimension['hidden'] = 'yes'
```

prs.title: feat: measures for agg_invoice_rows_exceptions_by_date
prs.description:
* adding measures to `agg_invoice_rows_exceptions_by_date`
* automatic generation by https://colab.research.google.com/drive/1bGO8AJI1nJ8OdN3U-z53NuzZ3i53AJGw?authuser=1#scrollTo=nyjjMyJf6xAT (request for access).

this is the main construction:

```python
def capitalise_first_letter(word):
  return word[0].upper() + word[1:]

def construct_measure(dimension, aggregation):
  measure = {
    'type': aggregation,
    'sql': "${"+dimension['name']+"}",
    'description': f"{capitalise_first_letter(aggregation)} of {dimension['description']}",
    'group_label': dimension['group_label'],
    'name': f"{aggregation}_{dimension['name']}",
    'tags': ["custom_content"]
  }

  return measure

measures = []

for dimension in lookml_json['views'][0]['dimensions']:
  if dimension['type'] == 'number':
    measures.append(construct_measure(dimension, 'sum'))
    measures.append(construct_measure(dimension, 'average'))
    dimension['hidden'] = 'yes'
```

```sh
Schema Mismatch for model mart_shipment_legs_revenue_recognition!!
            BigQuery refers to the model generated from running the dbt model (i.e. the SQL file.)
            dbt (or dbt Manifest) here refers to the columns named in the YAML file.
            There seems to be a mismatch between the schemas for these (BigQuery and dbt)
            Columns found in BigQuery not present in dbt:  matching_prices_invoice_weight.to_zone_price_list,matching_prices_invoice_weight.from_zone_price_list,illegitimate_amount_invoice_currency,illegitimate_amount_eur,matching_prices_backend_weight.shipment_purchase_rate_from_carrier_excl_vat,matching_prices_invoice_weight.price_list_max_weight_kg,total_duplicate_illegitimate_amount_invoice_currency,matching_prices_backend_weight.to_zone_price_list,matching_prices_backend_weight.price_list_max_weight_kg,matching_prices_backend_weight.shipment_base_rate_from_carrier_excl_vat,matching_prices_invoice_weight.shipment_base_rate_from_carrier_excl_vat,total_duplicate_illegitimate_amount_eur,total_illegitimate_amount_eur,matching_prices_invoice_weight.price_list_min_weight_kg,matching_prices_backend_weight.from_zone_price_list,matching_prices_invoice_weight.shipment_purchase_rate_from_carrier_excl_vat,matching_prices_backend_weight.shipment_sale_rate_excl_vat,total_illegitimate_amount_invoice_currency,revenue_recognition_date_on_prem,matching_prices_backend_weight.price_list_min_weight_kg
```

commits.messageBody:
* Add timestamp for last SC scan in delivery

After this timestamp parcel is expected to be on the way to the point or at the point

* Add timestamp for last out-for-delivery scan in delivery

This is the last driver out-for-delivery scan after which the parcel did not return to sorting center in delivery state

* Add timestamp for the last action after the last out-for-delivery scan

Even after out-for-delivery drivers may scan the bag or it may be redirected. This is important to note when looking for the first successful driver visit, because if the visit is successful but we still see these scans it means that the bag was not left at the shop

* Add table alias in select for CTEs

* Add filter of correct point for the bag scan timestamp

now bag scan is counted only for shipments scanned at correct last destination point and after all sorting center events in delivery

* Change driver drop-off timestamp to be based on shipment actions

Now it is checked that the drop-off is actually at the correct last destination point in delivery and after all sorting center actions

* Change first driver visit definition

Before driver visits were selected on the same day the parcel or bag was scanned. Now visits are selected after out-for-delivery action (or other driver scan or redirection after out-for-delivery if any). Also no more accounting for the late driver input if parcel was scanned before driver actually marked successful visit.

* Add columns for actions before shop delivery

Adding extra columns for timestamps in delivery of last sorting center scan, last out-for-delivery scan and any driver scans or redirections after it.

* fix last delivery SC scan

action_reason allows to filter out cases where parcel is actually on the way to return, but state still in delivery

* add intermediate cte with pre-shop scans

This way actions_after_out_for_delivery correctly represent out_for_delivery timestamp if no other actions are performed after out-for-delivery. Such logic allows for easier understanding of when to look for the first successful driver visit.

* Add location_type filter to SC scan

this filter ensures that action by the SC employee is not considered if shipment is with driver, point, or customers

* refine model description

Refine model description and column names

* fix join type

in driver_visits fixxed the logic regarding join

* add unit test

first unit test to mart_vcarrier_shop_kpis, but only covering newly added or modified columns

* add missing nodes for test

add dummy tables because they are required of the model

* fix mock csvs

ensuring that all mock csvs have needed columns

* rewrite logic for scans to decrease joins

the code is rewritten to use case statements instead of multiple joins. Also, added one column to see reported as missing parcels

* remove redundancy in case statements

Fixed case statements in pre_shop_scans, defined point_visits cte

* making poetry.lock the same as on main

* split actor_type

* add agg_by_date model

* new unit test

* fix incremental unit test

* add unit test agg_date_locker_actions

* adjust seed file

* adjust yml files and cte name

prs.title: feat: add columns to uncategorised rows
prs.description:
# Summary [Required]
_What & why is being changed. If applicable, how the change was validated & tested. Add links to Jira, PRs, Slack, Lucid, etc., if relevant._

there are some queries which are being executed in this [google sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1TUdJ4kRTZy70jfK7RyRkvSYUK_hfqNFqhlrI-MVagBw/edit#gid=1996908692) which query against `fct_invoice_rows`. as @jsakalyte suggested to finance stakeholders, there are opportunities to use the mart tables, where possible, to reduce the size of the data being queried.

some examples:

in Uncategorised Cost:

* `mart_uncategorised_invoice_rows` can be used if it had some additional columns.
* `invoice_amount_invoice_currency` and `invoice_id` needs to be added.
* `is_extra_cost` should not be used - prefer `cost_category = 'Extra cost'` instead.

```sql
  select 
      invoice_carrier_code, 
      invoice_date,
      invoice_id,
      cost_category,
      cost_sub_category,
      sum(case when is_extra_cost = false then invoice_amount_invoice_currency else 0 end) as sum_non_extra_cost_amount,
      sum(case when is_extra_cost = true then invoice_amount_invoice_currency else 0 end) as sum_extra_cost_amount,
      sum(invoice_amount_invoice_currency) as sum_total_invoice_amount 
    from dv-vgo-fin-prod.facts.fct_invoice_rows
    where  
      invoice_date = @INVOICE_DATE
      and (cost_category='uncategorised')
      and invoice_carrier_code != "USPS"
    group by 1,2,3,4,5
    order by 1																							
```

prs.title: fix: dao-dk unmatched fuel surcharges
prs.description:
# Summary [Required]

https://vinted.atlassian.net/browse/VGOFIN-24

* for DAO-DK, currently the fuel surcharge is presented as a lump sum.
* confirmed that for DAO-DK, the fuel surcharge can be allocated by proportion to the base cost (this is because the fuel surcharge is a % of the base cost).

this PR:
* allocates the fuel surcharge to each tracking code based on the fuel surcharge (assumes that there is a lump sum of fuel surcharge for every invoice and this is redistributed within the invoice.
* puts a test to ensure that the invoice cost description will only consist of the base cost and the fuel surcharge ('Diesel afgift linje') as the logic depends on this.

prs.title: fix: dpd-de, chronopost - accepted value test
prs.description:
# Summary [Required]

Addresses [CI failure](https://vinted.slack.com/archives/C041KP1LXGS/p1714799328344769) on 2025-04-05. See [Airflow Logs](https://791e254a41664da6a8b9df0215fc7ae7-dot-europe-west1.composer.googleusercontent.com/log?dag_id=vgo_finance_dag&execution_date=2024-05-03T05:00:00+00:00&map_index=-1&task_id=dbt_staging_layer).

The staging layer fails because there are new values, and therefore the accepted values test fails.

> [!NOTE]
> The reason why accepted values tests are enforced for these values is because they rely on the invoice cost description for determining key segregations (between base cost, the sign of the invoice amount, etc.). 
>
>However, if they happen too often and they are immaterial, we would turn them to warnings. For now, I propose keeping them as errors so we have a strong awareness of what is changing.

For DPD-DE (one new category - "address correction - foreign" - no impact)
```sql
with
    distinct_descriptions as (
        select distinct invoice_cost_description
        from `dv-vgo-fin-prod.staging.stg_carrier_invoices__dpd_de`
        order by invoice_cost_description
    )

select array_agg(concat("'", lower(invoice_cost_description), "',"))
from distinct_descriptions

```

For Chronopost (one new category - ESD - need to check what ESD means)
```sql
with
    distinct_descriptions as (
        select distinct invoice_cost_description
        from `dv-vgo-fin-prod.staging.stg_carrier_invoices__chronopost`
        order by invoice_cost_description
    )

select array_agg(concat("'", invoice_cost_description, "',"))
from distinct_descriptions
```

# To do list

- [ ] Follow up with finance to ask what ESD means.
- [ ] [Clear task in Airflow](https://791e254a41664da6a8b9df0215fc7ae7-dot-europe-west1.composer.googleusercontent.com/dags/vgo_finance_dag/grid?root=) to rerun tasks

prs.title: feat: monthly snapshots of mart_shipment_legs_customer_invoices and mart_historic_shipment_legs_revenue_recognition
prs.description:
# Summary

Arose from this request - see [Slack thread in dataverse-shipping-finance-use-cases](https://vinted.slack.com/archives/C068G84PPRD/p1714139289685489).

It was agreed:
> we create a snapshot of these two tables:
> * `mart_shipment_legs_customer_invoices`
> * `mart_shipment_legs_revenue_recognition`
>
> to start, i propose doing this 'snapshot' of the data once every month (i.e. ~on the first of every month~ on the second work day of the month, as per justina medziaustye's suggestion, we will have a snapshot of what existed in those marts).
>
> these snapshots will have a retention period of 10 years in line with the data retention requirements for accounting data (or if this is different, please let me know).
>
> we will not implement it as an incremental table with a high overwrite window because it does not fulfil the purpose of having a 'point in time' record of what we sent out.

Therefore, a snapshot of the lines where the customer invoice date is within the month and the revenue recognition date is within the last month (respectively) will be taken. Because it is necessary that the invoice is issued on the the **second working day** of the month, this will be the logic:

| Day of Week (1st) | 2nd Working Day  | CRON | Translation |
|-|-|-|-|
| Sun | Tue (3rd day of the Month) | `0 7 3 * 2` | At 07:00 on day-of-month 3 and on Tuesday. |
| Mon  | Tue (2nd day of the Month) | `0 7 2 * 2` | At 07:00 on day-of-month 2 and on Tuesday. |
| Tue | Wed (2nd day of the Month) | `0 7 2 * 3` | At 07:00 on day-of-month 2 and on Wednesday. |
| Wed  | Thu (2nd day of the Month) | `0 7 2 * 4` | At 07:00 on day-of-month 2 and on Thursday. |
| Thu | Fri (2nd day of the Month) | `0 7 2 * 5` | At 07:00 on day-of-month 2 and on Friday. |
| Fri | Mon (4th day of the Month) | `0 7 4 * 1` | At 07:00 on day-of-month 4 and on Monday. |
| Sat | Tue (4rd day of the month) | `0 7 4 * 2` | At 07:00 on day-of-month 4 and on Tuesday. |

This can be reduced to:

* Where first day of the month is Mon-Thu: `0 7 2 * 2-5`
* Where first day of the month is Fri-Sat: `0 7 4 * 1-2`
* Where first day of the month is Sun: `0 7 3 * 2`

For testing:
> The model has [generic dbt tests](https://github.com/vinted/dbt-unit-testing/tree/main?tab=readme-ov-file#usage) and/or other dbt tests ([dbt-utils](https://hub.getdbt.com/dbt-labs/dbt_utils/latest/), [dbt-expectations](https://hub.getdbt.com/calogica/dbt_expectations/latest/)) and/or [unit tests](https://github.com/vinted/dbt-unit-testing/tree/main?tab=readme-ov-file#usage).

I decide not to implement a unique test here because it will be unnecessary compute power.

prs.title: feat: introduce table to capture all price list join issues
prs.description: ## Description & motivation Stems from a request from the Finance Data Controlling team, to have visibility over the extent of invoices which do not join on the price list. See [original message](https://vinted.slack.com/archives/C068G84PPRD/p1714052284357719?thread_ts=1713423850.718599&cid=C068G84PPRD). > It would be interesting to see pricelist join failures month by month in % of all transactions and total count of failures (we do not really look into daily transactions for reporting reasons) This is in relation to the custom test created here: https://github.com/vinted/dataverse-vintedgo-dbt/pull/1383. The logic here adapts from the model `_union_all_test_failures` which was created in https://github.com/vinted/dataverse-vintedgo-dbt/pull/485. It is intentional that these models are not linked together, as there are many more lines of errors for this test compared to other tests (because we have a lower tolerance for price list unmatches). To keep the results of the other table meaningful, this is kept separate. > [!IMPORTANT] > A separate task is created as well to execute this model, as it should run daily after the completion of the daily task which runs this test, which is `dbt price list joining test` in `dag name: vgo_finance`. ## Expected results: We should have something that looks like: ```sql select * from test_failures.`carrier_invoice_test_price_lis*` order by test_utc_timestamp desc ``` ## Checklist: This checklist is mostly useful as a reminder of small things that can easily be forgotten – it is meant as a helpful tool rather than hoops to jump through. Put an `x` in all the items that apply, make notes next to any that haven't been addressed, and remove any items that are not relevant to this PR. - [x] My pull request represents one logical piece of work. - [x] My commits are related to the pull request and look clean. - [x] My PR contains tests, and they complete successfully - [x] My SQL follows the [style guide](https://vinted.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DPV2/pages/28012478596/Style+guide). - [x] I have materialized my models appropriately. - [x] I've added or updated the documentation of my models.

My comment is more about the test in general - I don't think it makes sense to aggregate it by invoice_file_name. All shipments should join to the price list, regardless of being invoiced by the carrier or not. 

Maybe it makes sense to add first/last_mile_carrier_id to the aggregation so we can report on that. 

At a later stage, it would be amazing if we can automate the reason for not joining (much like the fallback method, we can check which columns join to the price list and which ones don't) - so we know where it goes wrong

prs.title: feat: ups - use the primary tracking code when it's a return
prs.description:
## Description & motivation

There was evidence that the tracking code join rate was low on UPS invoices from 2024-04-22 and 2024-04-23. This was because UPS has a different tracking code for returns. The field which the model relied on, `tracking_number`, did not have values in our backend. Instead, this field was available in this field `place_holder_27`.

What this PR does is to:
- For returns, uses the original tracking number (in `place_holder_27`in UPS invoices) if available. Otherwise, fallback on tracking number.
- Amend the invoice cost description for `RTN` to differentiate it as a return. (This avoids it being flagged as a duplicate cost on the same tracking number)

## To-do before merge

Add new columns which appear to the [cost categorisation Google Sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1zwk64Nf4-1seTr17X1uvVZeYPLf62aaYRm-dKPS-6Pg/edit#gid=0):

```sql
select distinct
    case
        when charge_category_code = 'RTN'
        -- for returns, place_holder_27 is where the original tracking code,
        -- --> which we have in the backend, is tracked.
        then concat(charge_description, '-RTN')
        else charge_description
    end as charge_description_revised
from `dv-vgo-fin-prod.carrier_invoices.ups`
where charge_category_code = 'RTN'
;
```

Stage external sources in dev, and test:

```shell
dbt run-operation stage_external_sources --args "select: carrier_invoices.ups" --target dev --vars "ext_full_refresh: true"

dbt run-operation stage_external_sources --args "select: carrier_invoices.ups" --target test_samples --vars "ext_full_refresh: true"
```

## Validation of models:

There are joins with the codes which are available in `place_holder_27` from [files uploaded on 2024-04-23](https://console.cloud.google.com/storage/browser/_details/dv-vgo-fin-prod-csv-cleaner-output-bucket/ups/logic_v1/file_upload_date%3D2024-04-23/schema%3D222864e369/a0000f4101a-20240402_%281%29.parquet;tab=live_object?authuser=0&project=dv-vgo-fin-prod) - see:

```sql
with
    joining_keys as (
        select keys.*, invoice_carrier_code, shipment_tracking_code
        from
            dim_prep.dim_prep_shipment_carrier_legs_joining_keys as keys,
            unnest(invoice_carrier_codes) as invoice_carrier_code,
            unnest(shipment_tracking_codes) as shipment_tracking_code
    )

select *
from joining_keys
where
    shipment_created_at >= '2024-01-01'
    and invoice_carrier_code = 'UPS'
    -- these are codes which exist in place_holder_27
    and shipment_tracking_code in (
        '1ZF4101A6826164113',
        '1ZF4101A6889801244',
        '1ZF4101A6870269856',
        '1ZF4101A6841398100'
    )
;

```

should be dropped after merge, or whether a full-refresh run is required)

prs.title: chore: capitalise all from/to country fields
prs.description:
## Description & motivation

In the staging layer, `invoice_from_country_code` and `invoice_to_country_code` are populated where this information is available. I've noticed that the country codes can sometimes be capitalised, or in lowercase when running this query (below) for example. This is an attempt to standardise them all in uppercase:

```sql
with mart_prep_invoice_rows_wide_categories as (

    select *
    from marts_prep.mart_prep_invoice_rows_wide_categories
    where invoice_date = '2024-03-31'
),

get_most_common_from_to_country_code as (
    select
        invoice_id,
        invoice_carrier_code,
        invoice_currency,
        invoice_from_country_code,
        invoice_to_country_code,
        count(*) as count_rows,
        row_number() over(partition by invoice_id, invoice_carrier_code, invoice_currency order by count(*) desc) as row_number
    from mart_prep_invoice_rows_wide_categories
    group by all
    -- order by 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, row_number
    qualify row_number = 1

)

select *
from get_most_common_from_to_country_code;
```

prs.description: ## Description & motivation Failure in the `not_null` test for DPD PT's invoice date ([Slack thread](https://vinted.slack.com/archives/C06105W2T6F/p1713786827023059)). Failure because of the filename having extract characters behind the date. The offending filename was: ```shell 'gs://dv-vgo-fin-prod-csv-cleaner-output-bucket/dpd_pt/logic_v1/file_upload_date=2024-04-22/schema=684cfe9c6f/ft_38_6807_2023-12-31(1).parquet' ``` The `regexp_extract()` extracted `2023-12-31(1)`, which was unable to be parsed into a date with the `parse_date_multiple_formats()` macro. This PR gives a fix by taking the `invoice_date` using the following method: * Looks at the last 29 characters of the file name (observed length from all the file names). * Extracts the date with the pattern 'YYYY-MM-DD'. Checked that it has parsed all dates historically successfully: ```sql select invoice_file_name, regexp_extract(right(invoice_file_name, 30), r'(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})') as new_regex, replace( split(array_reverse(split(invoice_file_name, '/'))[safe_offset(0)], '_')[ safe_offset(3) ], '.parquet', '' ) as original_regex, count(*) as count_rows from `staging.stg_carrier_invoices__dpd_pt` group by all ``` Confirmed also that it works with the current offending invoice name: ```sql select 'gs://dv-vgo-fin-prod-csv-cleaner-output-bucket/dpd_pt/logic_v1/file_upload_date=2024-04-22/schema=684cfe9c6f/ft_38_6807_2023-12-31(1).parquet', regexp_extract( right( 'gs://dv-vgo-fin-prod-csv-cleaner-output-bucket/dpd_pt/logic_v1/file_upload_date=2024-04-22/schema=684cfe9c6f/ft_38_6807_2023-12-31(1).parquet', 30 ), r'(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})' ) as new_regex, replace( split( array_reverse( split( 'gs://dv-vgo-fin-prod-csv-cleaner-output-bucket/dpd_pt/logic_v1/file_upload_date=2024-04-22/schema=684cfe9c6f/ft_38_6807_2023-12-31(1).parquet', '/' ) )[safe_offset(0)], '_' )[safe_offset(3)], '.parquet', '' ) as old_regex, count(*) from `staging.stg_carrier_invoices__dpd_pt` group by all ``` This ensures the pipeline is more robust and will not fail in the future because of a similar error. ## Checklist: This checklist is mostly useful as a reminder of small things that can easily be forgotten – it is meant as a helpful tool rather than hoops to jump through. Put an `x` in all the items that apply, make notes next to any that haven't been addressed, and remove any items that are not relevant to this PR. - [x] My pull request represents one logical piece of work. - [x] My commits are related to the pull request and look clean. - [x] My PR contains tests, and they complete successfully - [x] My SQL follows the [style guide](https://vinted.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DPV2/pages/28012478596/Style+guide). - [x] I've added or updated the documentation of my models.

prs.title: fix: evri - dealing with 2nd shipment attempts
prs.description:
## Description & motivation

For EVRI-UK shipments, there were cases where 2nd shipments were being flagged as dupllicates.

As shared by @ArabellaCM, the two queries showed the results. In this case, it is unlikely that they were duplicate charges as the dates were different. Yet, in `fct_invoice_rows`, the logic to flag duplicates looks at the `shipment_carrier_leg_id` and the `invoice_cost_description` to determine if there were duplicates.

The following queries shows the errors:
```sql
select * from dv-vgo-fin-prod.carrier_invoices.evri where parcel_number = 'H00IAA0752981188'
```

![image](https://github.com/vinted/dataverse-vintedgo-dbt/assets/38421339/8412cc1b-9e1a-4710-8144-680a61040138)

In this case, we found that the 2nd shipments could be identified using a pattern where the custom reference was `0`. To deal with this, we concatenate the cost description with this 0 to identify this as a second shipment.

## Validation of models:

There are four new categories which appear, that should be added to the [Cost Categorisation Google Sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1zwk64Nf4-1seTr17X1uvVZeYPLf62aaYRm-dKPS-6Pg/edit#gid=0):

| Network Undelivered LL |          | 100      |

| courier                |          | 139773   |

| hi  (additional)                     | missing  | 17       |

| ni  (additional)                     | missing  | 337      |

prs.title: feat: add column-level tests for fct_invoice_row
prs.description: ## Test 1: Check on Dates Observed there are invoice dates which were in 2024-11 and 2024-12, which was an anomaly. This arose from INPOST-PL invoices, where the dates were not parsed correctly (due to a US-formatted invoice). The issue was addressed and is resolved in https://github.com/vinted/dataverse-vintedgo-dbt/pull/1397. Nonetheless, a test should be introduced to detect such errors and cause a failure to the DAG if it does not satisfy the condition. The test will determine if the invoice date does not exceed the last day of the current month. The SQL code used to find it: ```sql select invoice_carrier_code, extract(year from invoice_date) as year, extract(month from invoice_date) as month, count(*) as count from facts.fct_invoice_rows where invoice_date >= date_add(last_day(current_date()), interval 1 day) group by all ``` ## Test 2: Check on Currencies This PR also adds a check on the currencies which are coming from the invoices. If there is a new currency which is not in the marketplace table (`dv-mkp-fin-prod.marts.currency_conversions_long_format`) which is used for currency conversions, this test will fail. To check for the currencies available, use the query: ```sql select distinct from_currency from dv-mkp-fin-prod.marts.currency_conversions_long_format order by 1 ``` If it fails, please contact the Marketplace Finance AEs. ## To-do before merge - [x] Ensure PR https://github.com/vinted/dataverse-vintedgo-dbt/pull/1397 is merged ## Checklist: This checklist is mostly useful as a reminder of small things that can easily be forgotten – it is meant as a helpful tool rather than hoops to jump through. prs.title: fix: missing information in dpd-pl rows
prs.description: ## Description & motivation The test `invoice_test_not_null` was failing for `DPD-PL` invoices as there was an unexpected invoice format. The carrier itemises their services, and provides the breakdown in `cena_netto` or `price`, but we were using `kwota` or `total_price` initially. This PR makes an amendment to the logic such that: * We will have a breakdown of the invoice costs (typically energy fee is the second line). * Issues raised by test `invoice_test_not_null` is addressed. The approach was discussed ([Slack thread](https://vinted.slack.com/archives/C068G84PPRD/p1712829939506669)) and agreed with finance stakeholders as they would like to see the breakdown. prs.title: refactor: mart_prep_invoice_rows_wide_categories
prs.description: Refactors `mart_prep_invoice_rows_wide_categories` created in https://github.com/vinted/dataverse-vintedgo-dbt/pull/1284. Similar to refactoring which was done in https://github.com/vinted/dataverse-vintedgo-dbt/pull/1339, this refactoring aims to reduce the slot time used. Joins on aggregated data are more expensive than window functions. This is because there is a shuffling off data implies significant data movement across nodes during query execution which increases the slot time used. There are two refactoring changes: * Instead of join on pivoted versions of `fct_invoice_rows`, a window function is used instead. * The computation for null invoice descriptions is done in the first CTE, to minimise recomputation. On the premise we are [billed by slot time](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/pricing) used, the approach of using window functions has significant reductions in slot time consumed, and is expected to be cheaper: Using pivot and joins (current): Using window function (proposed in this PR) - **41% reduction in the slot time**:

prs.title: feat: is_hvf_now uses gmv first
prs.description:
As mentioned in this [Slack thread](https://vinted.slack.com/archives/C02JMNFS9GD/p1712154221399449?thread_ts=1712148630.086939&cid=C02JMNFS9GD) and highlighted in this [Jupyter Notebook](https://jupyter.ams1.int.vinted.com/hub/user-redirect/lab/tree/agne.misiukonyte/%23%20everyday%20random.ipynb), there are items which are flagged as HVF when sold (i.e. `is_high_value_fashion_now = true`) when the `gmv_eur` is <= 100 EUR. This should not be the case.

There are different informational needs:
* HVF criterion met at item listing (`original_price`): this is the definition used vinted-wide to refer to a 'HVF item'.
* HVF criterion met before offer as made (`price`): this is the definition used to determine IVS eligibility
* HVF criterion met when sold (`gmv`): this is what buyer domain / marketing is interested in - which the current definition doesn't meet.

The issue:
* Currently, `is_high_value_fashion_now` only takes into account the latest listing price, but not the GMV. 
* There are some transformations done (see `ItemSaleFact`) to derive the GMV.

This is the transformation:
```scala
        "items.price", // item price at the time of sale
        "transactions.offer_discount", // from TransactionSaleFact
         // item price proportional to offer discount
        "(1-transactions.offer_discount) * items.price as gmv",
```

Based on the intent of what `is_high_value_fashion_now` is supposed to represent, the GMV should be assessed first (if available), before looking at the latest listing price. (i.e. (coalesce(`gmv_eur, latest_listing_price_eur)`).

This PR:
1. Incorporates this logic
2. Creates a new flag for `is_high_value_fashion_before_sold`

# What needs to be done post-merge:

[ ] Revise definition of `is_high_value_fashion_now` in`vinted.warehouse.jobs.growth.dimensions.ItemDimensions`.
[ ] Add the new flag downstream (e.g. in `ListingEnrichedFact`)
prs.author: jeremychia

prs.title: Adjust weekly targets (HVF) to account for OVS Launches
prs.description:
_Domain: Programs_

Context:

* Monthly targets are converted to weekly targets taking into account historical (last 8 years) trends.
* This logic distributes values throughout the entire month.
* There are some countries where OVS Launch is in the middle of the month. Therefore, weekly targets should also reflect this.

What this PR does:

* Adjusts the logic such that if the date is before the launch date, the weight given to that date is zero.
* Applies this to the fields:

- `sold_items_with_ovs_incl_rejections`
- `total_listings_ovs_eligible`
- `sold_items_ovs_eligible`
- `sold_items_with_ovs_excl_rejections`

prs.title: Freeze weekly (HVF) targets
prs.description:
_Domain: Programs_

It was reported that the weekly targets calculation logic resulted in moving targets (@JurgitaSakalyte).

This was because the basis period used to distribute weights would be moving based on the period of modelling. 

This change aims to fix the moving logic by fixing the number of historical periods for which the weights are based on to 8 periods before the respective target period. (e.g. for 2024, it will look at 2023 and the preceding 7 years). This will ensure that there are no amendments in the target weights unless there is a change in the underlying data, which is unlikely.

prs.title: chore: remove filters on warehouse jobs, move filter to looker explore instead
prs.description:
_Domain: Programs_

Previously, these filters were implemented to filter out information from daily high value fashion aggregates on the warehouse jobs - this was with the view of limiting the data to improve Looker performance. These were done in:

* https://github.com/vinted/warehouse-jobs/pull/13213
* https://github.com/vinted/warehouse-jobs/pull/13221

For the calculation of historical weekly data, however, this meant that the time horizon was limited only to '2020-01-01' and onwards. We wanted to have a long time horizon to start from at least 8 years before the targets started for a proper comparison.

Therefore, these filters in the warehouse-jobs will be undone. The filter will instead be introduced in Looker to help limit the data and ensure performance is stable by reducing the size of the dataset read.

See https://github.com/vinted/lookml/pull/2524 for associated PR.

prs.title: Fix: Missing original prices in HVF Item Dimensions
prs.description:
_Domain: Programs_

As part of a report from @JurgitaSakalyte that there were missing buyer segmentations for sales with IVS, I looked into the detailed level of items, their status, and the bearing it had on this buyer segmentation. I found that there were items which should have been classified as HVF but were not because of a missing `original_price_eur` from the price used in `ItemImportedDimensions`.

This is because of a backend error, which had a fix in `ItemDimensions` (see below under [1] for details). There were 10104 impacted items (0.05% of all HVF items):

```
with
    details as (
        select
            sale.portal,
            sale.item_id,
            sale.local_time,
            sale.item_original_listing_price_eur,
            sale.item_comparison_category_high_value_fashion,
            sale.item_is_high_value_fashion_on_listing_creation,
            sale.offline_verification_check,
            sale.selling_way,
            hvf_user.buyer_segmentation
        from enriched_facts.item_sale as sale
        left join
            dimensions.high_value_fashion_user_dimension as hvf_user
            on sale.portal = hvf_user.portal
            and sale.buyer_id = hvf_user.id
        where
            sale.item_original_listing_price_eur >= 100
            and sale.item_comparison_category_high_value_fashion is not null
            and item_is_high_value_fashion_on_listing_creation = false
    )

select *
from details
order by local_time desc
limit 100
;

```


This PR does the following:

[1]

Introduces a consistent logic used in `ItemDimensions` (see [L328-334](https://github.com/vinted/warehouse-jobs/blob/revise-weekly-intrapolated-targets/spark/src/main/scala/vinted/warehouse/jobs/growth/dimensions/ItemDimension.scala#L328-L334)) to write the original price as the latest price if the listing date was before 2019-11-06, when a backend fix was implemented. This makes consistent the prices used in `HighValueFashionItemDimension` (HVF Item Dim) to determine whether an item was an HVF Item or not.

Because the HVF Item Dim is used to determine user dimensions downstream, it is necessary to align the price information to ensure consistent categorisation.

Recommend that prospective backend fixes should be done as upstream as possible prospectively. (i.e. in this case where the logic fix is implemented in `ItemDimension` only, this results in cases like these. However, because of the number of dependencies on `ItemImportedDimension`, I will not implement the fix here but instead recommend that this will be fixed in the Dataverse).

[2]

Refactoring - as the spot rates were introduced in `ItemImportedDimensions` in this PR (https://github.com/vinted/warehouse-jobs/pull/11949),
prs.author: jeremychia

prs.title: HVF Weekly Targets vs Actuals
prs.description:
_Domain: Programs_

This PR introduces a first iteration of the HVF Weekly Targets vs Actuals comparison.

For actuals:
* Year-week aggregates will be performed on listing, item sales, and competitors' listings aggregates.
 * In order to do a weekly aggregates, the competitor's view aggregation was adjusted (in this revision (https://github.com/vinted/warehouse-jobs/pull/12943/commits/03f88af2c4e0384e51c362aecc2347a699e067c3), `HighValueFashionCompetitorsView` will return daily data, and the monthly and weekly aggregation will be performed downstream). Performed check to confirm no other model uses this view, and is therefore not affected.

For targets:
* In the first iteration, the monthly targets will be distributed equally across the number of days within a given month. 
* There will be subsequent iterations to account for seasonality and holidays.

For more information, see this [Google Document](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1glNfkDDenAL0EB2RdvLkM8p4Z0Zvl78UW0ZgAk3VbIk/edit).

Once live, the model for `WeeklyHighValueFashionTargetVsActualAggregates` will be exposed to Looker, similar to the monthly comparison.
prs.author: jeremychia

reviews.body: Very nice, and done super fast, thanks Jeremy 👍

prs.title: feat: introduce vestiaire_listings_aggregated + vc_listings adjusted
prs.description:
## Description & motivation

The goal is to have the number of Vestiaire (VC) listings by listing date, country code, and price group (`price_eur_binned`). This for the purpose of having actuals versus targets comparisons for High Value Fashion. See [refinement](https://docs.google.com/document/d/10fpfiwKzk82V0u9lIGNxL7q4aT0nbTN_eI6CGIvZNXg/edit#heading=h.gdznkbjfml0f).

The following downstream steps will be done:

* This table will be ingested into Vinted's on-prem DWH.
* It will be added as part of the HVF actuals versus target comparison (see [MonthlyHighValueFashionTargetVsActualAggregates](https://github.com/vinted/warehouse-jobs/blob/master/spark/src/main/scala/vinted/warehouse/jobs/growth/aggregates/MonthlyHighValueFashionTargetVsActualAggregates.scala) in warehouse-jobs).
* This information will represents`total_listings_vestiaire_collective` in the table.

Brief description on implementation:

* As agreed (see [Slack thread](https://vinted.slack.com/archives/C05G1RGB7DL/p1703692769009779) in comp-intel-data-internal), `mart_competitors_listings_aggregated` is used as a basis for calculating the number of  VClistings.
* It is assumed that all categories of Vestiaire listings are relevant for this computation.
* Because there are 1.33% of listings to date that do not have a price group, these are distributed proportionately by listing date, country code.

In addition:

* This PR removes the dummy model created while creating the aggregates layer in https://github.com/vinted/dataverse-marketplace-dbt/pull/1035.
prs.author: jeremychia

reviews.body:
Hey! Looks good. Two considerations:

* Consider adding this model not to `mart` but to `aggregates` (a layer that doesn't exist yet, but we can configure quite easily)
* Consider moving the distribution logic to a macro. Two reasons: (1) cleans up code here, (2) enables potential future users to also re-use the code.

For the rest: couple of renaming comments for your considerations!
lgtm
